learn.hook: A rangoli tile, a kite and a roti are all flat shapes. Can you count their sides and corners?
points: A 2D shape is flat. You can draw it on paper.
A side is a straight line on the edge of a shape. A corner is where two sides meet.
Triangle: 3 sides. Square and rectangle: 4 sides. Pentagon: 5 sides. Hexagon: 6 sides.
A circle has one curved edge and no corners.
In a closed shape made of straight sides, the number of sides and corners is the same.

example.q: Kabir draws a hexagon and a triangle. How many sides do they have altogether?

learn.reallife: Look at floor tiles, a carrom board, road signs and a kite. Each one is a flat shape you can name by counting its sides.

games.title: Match the shape to its sides

quiz.q: How many sides does a hexagon have?
quiz.explain: A hexagon has 6 straight sides and 6 corners.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the hexagon with the pentagon or octagon

quiz.q: A rangoli tile has 5 straight sides. What is the name of this shape?
quiz.explain: A flat shape with 5 straight sides is a pentagon.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the names pentagon and hexagon

quiz.q: How many corners does a circle have?
quiz.explain: A circle has one curved edge and no corners at all.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the start point of a drawn circle is a corner

quiz.q: Riya joins 3 straight sticks end to end to make a closed shape. Which shape does she get?
quiz.explain: 3 straight sides joined in a closed shape make a triangle.
quiz.mistake: Does not link the number of sides to the shape name

quiz.q: Arjun draws 2 triangles and 1 square. How many sides is that altogether?
quiz.explain: Each triangle has 3 sides and the square has 4. 3 + 3 + 4 = 10.
quiz.mistake: Counts only one triangle

quiz.q: Which of these is a flat 2D shape?
quiz.explain: A square drawn on paper is flat. A ball, a dice and a tin are solid 3D objects.
quiz.mistake: Thinks any object with a square face is a 2D shape

quiz.q: Kabir draws a square with each side 5 cm long. What is the total length of all its sides?
quiz.explain: A square has 4 equal sides. 5 + 5 + 5 + 5 = 20 cm.
steps: A square has 4 sides of 5 cm
quiz.mistake: Adds only two sides, or multiplies 5 by 5

quiz.q: Meena counts all the corners of one square and one triangle. How many corners does she count?
quiz.explain: A square has 4 corners and a triangle has 3 corners. 4 + 3 = 7.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a triangle has 4 corners

teach.ask: Gappu is puzzled! How do I know if a flat shape is a triangle, a square or a hexagon?
teach.praise: Wow! Count the sides and corners and the shape tells you its name. Gappu gets it now!
teach.nudge: What should Gappu count on the shape to find its name?

topics.title: Solid 3D shapes: faces, edges and corners

learn.hook: A laddoo rolls, but a dice does not. Why? Let us find out!
points: A 3D shape is solid. It has length, width and height. You can hold it.
A face is a flat surface. An edge is where two faces meet. A corner is where edges meet.
A cube (like a dice) has 6 square faces, 12 edges and 8 corners.
A cuboid (like a brick) also has 6 faces, 12 edges and 8 corners.
A sphere (like a laddoo) is round all over. A cylinder (like a tin) has 2 flat faces and a curved surface. A cone (like a party cap) has 1 flat face and a pointed tip.

example.q: A matchbox is a cuboid. How many faces, edges and corners does it have?
steps: Count the flat faces: top, bottom, front, back, left, right = 6
Count the edges: 4 on top, 4 on the bottom, 4 standing = 12
Count the corners: 4 on top and 4 on the bottom = 8

learn.reallife: Your geometry box is a cuboid, a ball is a sphere, a pipe is a cylinder and an ice-cream cone is a cone.

games.title: Match the object to its 3D shape
True or false?
items: A cube has 6 square faces: top, bottom and 4 around.
A sphere is round all over, so it has no corners.
Its curved surface lets it roll when it lies on its side.
A cone has only 1 flat face, the circle at its bottom.
Every face of a cube is a square.
All 6 faces of a cube are equal squares.
4 edges on top, 4 on the bottom and 4 standing up make 12.

quiz.q: How many faces does a dice shaped like a cube have?
quiz.explain: A cube has 6 faces. That is why a dice has the numbers 1 to 6.
quiz.mistake: Counts only the faces that can be seen at one time

quiz.q: How many edges does a cube have?
quiz.explain: A cube has 4 edges on top, 4 on the bottom and 4 standing up. 4 + 4 + 4 = 12.
quiz.mistake: Counts corners (8) instead of edges

quiz.q: How many corners does a matchbox shaped like a cuboid have?
quiz.explain: A cuboid has 4 corners on top and 4 on the bottom. 4 + 4 = 8.
quiz.mistake: Counts faces (6) or edges (12) instead of corners

quiz.q: Which shape can roll in every direction and has no flat face?
quiz.explain: A sphere is curved all over. It has no flat face, so it rolls any way.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a cylinder has no flat faces because it can roll

quiz.q: A tin of oil is shaped like which 3D shape?
quiz.explain: A tin has a circle at the top, a circle at the bottom and a curved side. That is a cylinder.
quiz.mistake: Names the 2D circle face instead of the 3D shape

quiz.q: How many flat faces does a cylinder have?
quiz.explain: A cylinder has 2 flat circle faces, one at the top and one at the bottom. Its side is curved, not flat.
quiz.mistake: Counts the curved side as a flat face

quiz.q: Which 3D shape has one flat circle face and one pointed tip?
quiz.explain: A cone, like a party cap, has a circle at the bottom and a pointed tip at the top.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the cone and the cylinder

quiz.q: Joseph has 2 dice. How many faces do the 2 dice have altogether?
quiz.explain: Each dice has 6 faces. 6 + 6 = 12.
quiz.mistake: Counts the faces of only one dice

teach.ask: Gappu found a dice and a laddoo. How are these solid shapes different? Please explain!
teach.praise: Super! Faces, edges and corners help me tell solid shapes apart. Gappu is a shape expert now!
teach.nudge: What can Gappu count on a dice? Think about faces, edges or corners.

learn.hook: Open up a sweet box and lay it flat. What shape do you get? That flat shape is called a net!
points: A net is a flat shape that can be folded to make a 3D shape.
The net of a cube has 6 squares. The net of a cuboid has 6 rectangles.
The net of a cylinder has 2 circles and 1 rectangle.
The net of a square pyramid has 1 square and 4 triangles.
The top view is what you see from straight above. The front view is what you see from the front.

example.q: A glass shaped like a cylinder stands on a table. What do you see from the top and from the front?
steps: From straight above, you see the round rim: a circle.
From the front, you see a straight side, top and bottom: a rectangle.
example.answer: Top view: circle. Front view: rectangle.

learn.reallife: Sweet boxes, gift boxes and toothpaste boxes are made by folding flat cardboard nets.

games.title: Match the net to its shape

items.text: The top view of a glass standing on a table is a ___.
The front view of a party cap standing on a table is a ___.
The top view of a dice on a table is a ___.
The front view of a glass standing on a table is a ___.

quiz.q: How many squares are there in the net of a cube?
quiz.explain: A cube has 6 square faces, so its net has 6 squares.
quiz.mistake: Forgets the top or bottom face

quiz.q: A net has 2 circles and 1 rectangle. What does it fold into?
quiz.explain: The rectangle rolls into the curved side and the 2 circles close the top and bottom. That is a cylinder.
quiz.mistake: Thinks any net with circles makes a cone

quiz.q: Aisha looks at a glass standing upright from straight above. What shape does she see?
quiz.explain: From the top she sees the round rim of the glass, which is a circle.
quiz.mistake: Gives the front view instead of the top view

quiz.q: A party cap shaped like a cone stands on its base. What is its front view?
quiz.explain: From the front, the cap goes from a wide bottom to a point at the top. It looks like a triangle.
quiz.mistake: Gives the top view (circle) instead of the front view

quiz.q: Kabir looks at a laddoo from the top, the front and the side. What shape does he see every time?
quiz.explain: A laddoo is a sphere. A sphere looks like a circle from every direction.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the view changes for a round ball

quiz.q: A net has 1 square and 4 triangles. What does it fold into?
quiz.explain: The square is the base and the 4 triangles fold up to meet at a point. That is a square pyramid.
quiz.mistake: Sees the square and thinks of a cube

quiz.q: Meena cuts open a cereal box shaped like a cuboid and lays it flat. How many rectangles are in the net?
quiz.explain: A cuboid has 6 faces: top, bottom, front, back and 2 sides. So the net has 6 rectangles.
quiz.mistake: Forgets the top and bottom faces

quiz.q: Harpreet looks at a dice lying on a table from straight above. What shape does she see?
quiz.explain: The top face of a dice is a square, so the top view is a square.
quiz.mistake: Guesses without picturing the top face

teach.ask: Gappu has a flat piece of card with squares on it. How can it become a box? And what is a top view?
teach.praise: Yes! A net folds up into a solid shape, and a view is what you see from one side. Gappu will make a box now!
teach.nudge: What do we do to a flat net to make it a 3D shape?

learn.hook: A bird on a tree and an ant on the ground look at the same bucket. Do they see the same shape?
points: The same object can look different from the top, the front and the side.
The top view is what you see from straight above, like a bird.
The front view is what you see when you stand in front of it.
From one side you see only that side. Things on the other side stay hidden.
A ball looks like a circle from every direction. A dice looks like a square from every direction.

example.q: Riya stacks 3 cubes one on top of the other to make a tower. What does she see from the top and from the front?
steps: From straight above, only the top cube's face shows: 1 square.
From the front, all 3 cubes show, one above the other: 3 squares in a column.
example.answer: Top: 1 square. Front: 3 squares in a column.

learn.reallife: Maps and drone photos show places from the top. A photo of your house from the road shows its front view.

games.title: Match the view to the shape
pairs: A standing glass from the front
A party cap from the front

games.title: True or false?
items: From the top, a cone standing on its base looks like a circle.
Looking down, you see its round base with the tip in the middle.
A dice looks like a circle from the top.
Every face of a dice is a square, so the top view is a square.
From one side of a car, you can see all 4 of its wheels.
From one side you see only the 2 wheels on that side.
Top view means looking from straight above.
Like a bird looking down from the sky.
The front view and the top view of a cube are both squares.
All faces of a cube are squares, so every view is a square.
A ball looks like a triangle from the side.
A ball is a sphere, which looks like a circle from every side.

quiz.q: From straight above, what shape does a bucket standing upright look like?
quiz.explain: Looking down into a bucket you see its round rim, which is a circle.
quiz.mistake: Gives the side view of the bucket

quiz.q: Arjun stands in front of a tall water tank shaped like a cylinder. What shape does he see?
quiz.explain: From the front, a standing cylinder has a straight side, a flat top and a flat bottom, so it looks like a rectangle.
quiz.mistake: Gives the top view (circle) instead of the front view

quiz.q: Aisha looks at a car from one side. How many wheels can she see?
quiz.explain: A car has 2 wheels on each side. From one side the other 2 wheels are hidden.
quiz.mistake: Counts all the wheels the car has, not the ones she can see

quiz.q: Kabir stacks 4 cubes one on top of the other. Looking from straight above, how many cube faces can he see?
quiz.explain: From the top he sees only the top face of the highest cube. The others are hidden below it.
quiz.mistake: Counts all the cubes in the tower

quiz.q: Kabir looks at the same tower of 4 cubes from the front. How many squares does he see?
quiz.explain: From the front, every cube in the tower shows one face. So he sees 4 squares, one above the other.
quiz.mistake: Gives the top view answer

quiz.q: A bird flying over a house sees its roof. What do we call this view?
quiz.explain: Looking from straight above is called the top view.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the names of the views

quiz.q: Which object looks like a circle from the top AND a rectangle from the front?
quiz.explain: A glass is a cylinder: round from the top, rectangle from the front. A ball is a circle both ways, a dice is a square, and a cap is a triangle from the front.
quiz.mistake: Checks only one of the two views

quiz.q: Meena holds a round steel plate flat and looks at it exactly from the side, at eye level. What does she see?
quiz.explain: A plate is very thin. From the side you see only its thin edge, like a flat strip.
quiz.mistake: Gives the top view of the plate

teach.ask: Gappu saw a glass from the top and from the front and got two different shapes! How can one glass look like two shapes?
teach.praise: Now I see! Where you look from changes the shape you see. Thank you!
teach.nudge: Does it matter where Gappu is looking from? Tell me about top and front.

topics.title: Spatial thinking: blocks, places and directions

learn.hook: Can you count blocks you cannot even see? Let's play hide and seek with cubes!
points: In a stack, some blocks hide behind or under others. Count row by row and layer by layer.
A wall that is 4 cubes long and 2 cubes high has 4 + 4 = 8 cubes.
Left and right change when you turn around. Things that were on your right are now on your left.
On most maps North is at the top, South at the bottom, East on the right and West on the left.
Position words like in front, behind, above, below, left and right help us find things.

example.q: Arjun builds steps: 3 cubes in the bottom row, 2 in the middle row and 1 on top. How many cubes did he use?

learn.reallife: Shopkeepers stack boxes in layers. Auto drivers use left, right and map directions to find your house.

items.text: If you turn around, things on your right are now on your ___.
On a map with North at the top, South is at the ___.
On a map with North at the top, East is on the ___.
Steps made of 2 cubes with 1 cube on top use ___ cubes.

quiz.q: A wall of cubes is 5 cubes long and 2 cubes high. How many cubes are in the wall?
quiz.explain: Each row has 5 cubes and there are 2 rows. 5 + 5 = 10.
quiz.mistake: Adds the length and height instead of counting every row

quiz.q: Steps are built with 4 cubes at the bottom, then 3, then 2, then 1 on top. How many cubes in all?
quiz.explain: Add every row: 4 + 3 + 2 + 1 = 10.
quiz.mistake: Forgets the single cube on top

quiz.q: Riya faces the school gate and the library is on her right. She turns around to face the other way. Where is the library now?
quiz.explain: When you turn around, left and right swap. So the library is now on her left.
quiz.mistake: Thinks left and right stay the same after turning around

quiz.q: Joseph builds a block with 2 layers. Each layer has 2 rows of 2 cubes. How many cubes did he use?
quiz.explain: One layer has 2 × 2 = 4 cubes. Two layers have 4 + 4 = 8 cubes, even though some are hidden inside.
quiz.mistake: Counts only the cubes that can be seen

quiz.q: 7 children stand in a row. Meena is 3rd from the left. What is her place counting from the right?
quiz.explain: There are 2 children to her left, so there are 7 - 3 = 4 children to her right. She comes next, so she is 5th from the right.
quiz.mistake: Subtracts 7 - 3 and forgets to count Meena herself

quiz.q: On a map, North is at the top. Which direction is on the right side of the map?
quiz.explain: With North at the top, East is on the right, West on the left and South at the bottom.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up East and West

quiz.q: Harpreet looks in a mirror and raises her right hand. If the girl in the mirror were a real girl facing Harpreet, which of her hands would be up?
quiz.explain: A mirror flips left and right. The girl in the mirror faces Harpreet, so the raised hand is her left hand.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a mirror image is exactly the same as the real person

quiz.q: Kabir walks 4 steps forward and then 4 steps back. How many steps away from the start is he?
quiz.explain: Going 4 steps back undoes the 4 steps forward. He is back at the start, 0 steps away.
quiz.mistake: Adds the steps instead of seeing they cancel out

teach.ask: Gappu built a big block of cubes, but some cubes are hidden inside. How can Gappu count them all?
teach.praise: Brilliant! Count each layer and add them up, hidden cubes too. Gappu counted all of them!
teach.nudge: What about the cubes Gappu cannot see? How can we count those?

learn.hook: 5, 10, 15, 20... Can you guess the next number before your friend does?
points: A number pattern follows a rule, again and again.
Some patterns add the same number each time: 3, 7, 11, 15 adds 4.
Some patterns take away the same number: 50, 45, 40 takes away 5.
Some patterns double: 2, 4, 8, 16.
Some patterns grow by a bit more each time: 1, 3, 6, 10 adds 2, then 3, then 4.

example.q: Find the next number: 4, 9, 14, 19, ?

learn.reallife: House numbers on one side of a street often go 1, 3, 5, 7. Bus timings like 8:00, 8:15, 8:30 follow a pattern too.

games.title: Build the pattern
games.prompt: Put these in order to make a count-by-12 pattern

quiz.q: What comes next? 5, 10, 15, 20, ?
quiz.explain: Each number is 5 more than the one before. 20 + 5 = 25.
quiz.mistake: Adds 1 to the last number instead of following the rule

quiz.q: What comes next? 3, 7, 11, 15, ?
quiz.explain: The rule is add 4. 15 + 4 = 19.
quiz.mistake: Adds 3 or 5 instead of finding the real gap

quiz.q: What comes next? 50, 45, 40, 35, ?
quiz.explain: The numbers go down by 5 each time. 35 - 5 = 30.
quiz.mistake: Adds 5 instead of taking away 5

quiz.q: What comes next? 2, 4, 8, 16, ?
quiz.explain: Each number is double the one before. 16 × 2 = 32.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the rule is add 2 because 2 to 4 adds 2

quiz.q: Find the missing number: 100, 200, 300, ?, 500
quiz.explain: The numbers go up by 100. After 300 comes 400.
quiz.mistake: Adds 10 instead of 100

quiz.q: Riya saves ₹10 on Day 1, ₹20 on Day 2 and ₹30 on Day 3. If the pattern goes on, how much does she save on Day 5?
quiz.explain: She saves ₹10 more each day: ₹40 on Day 4 and ₹50 on Day 5.
quiz.mistake: Finds Day 4 instead of Day 5

quiz.q: What comes next? 1, 3, 6, 10, ?
quiz.explain: The jumps grow by 1 each time: +2, +3, +4, so next is +5. 10 + 5 = 15.
quiz.mistake: Adds 4 again instead of seeing the jump grow

quiz.q: What comes next? 9, 18, 27, 36, ?
quiz.explain: This is the 9 times table. 36 + 9 = 45.
quiz.mistake: Adds 8 or 10 instead of 9, or adds only 1 to 36

teach.ask: Gappu sees 6, 12, 18, 24 on a wall. How can Gappu find the next number?
teach.praise: Yes! Find the rule and use it again to get the next number. Gappu says 30!
teach.nudge: What is the same between each pair of numbers? Is there a rule?

learn.hook: Rangoli, bangles and border designs repeat in beautiful ways. Spot the part that repeats!
points: A repeating pattern has a core: a small group that repeats again and again.
In 🔺🔵🔺🔵, the core is 🔺🔵 and it has 2 parts.
To find a far-away item, use the core. If the core has 3 parts, the 9th item is the last one of the core.
A growing pattern gets bigger each step, like 1, 3, 5, 7 dots.
Shapes can also turn in a pattern, a quarter turn each time.

example.q: Bead pattern: red, red, blue, red, red, blue... What colour is the 12th bead?
steps: The core is red, red, blue: 3 beads.
12 ÷ 3 = 4, so the 12th bead ends the 4th core.
The last bead of the core is blue.

learn.reallife: Look at saree borders, mehendi designs and floor tiles. They are full of repeating and growing patterns.

games.title: Pattern facts
items: In ⭐🌙⭐🌙, the core that repeats is ⭐🌙.
A growing pattern stays the same size every step.
A growing pattern gets bigger each step.
1 dot, 3 dots, 5 dots, 7 dots is a growing pattern.
In red, blue, red, blue, the 10th bead is red.
Red is at places 1, 3, 5... (odd). 10 is even, so it is blue.
After 4 quarter turns, a shape is back where it started.
4 quarter turns make one full turn.

quiz.q: Which shape comes next? Triangle, circle, triangle, circle, triangle, ?
quiz.explain: The core is triangle, circle. After a triangle comes a circle.
quiz.mistake: Repeats the last shape instead of following the core

quiz.q: Aisha's bead string goes red, red, blue, red, red, blue... What colour is the 9th bead?
quiz.explain: The core has 3 beads. 9 ÷ 3 = 3, so the 9th bead is the end of a core, which is blue.
steps: The last bead of each core is blue
quiz.mistake: Thinks red comes most often so it must be red

quiz.q: How many beads are in the core of this pattern? 🟡🟢🟢🟡🟢🟢🟡🟢🟢
quiz.explain: 🟡🟢🟢 repeats again and again. It has 3 beads.
quiz.mistake: Counts all the beads instead of only the repeating part

quiz.q: Kabir makes squares of tiles: 1 by 1, then 2 by 2, then 3 by 3. How many tiles does the 4 by 4 square need?
quiz.explain: A 4 by 4 square has 4 rows of 4 tiles. 4 × 4 = 16.
quiz.mistake: Adds 4 + 4 instead of making 4 rows of 4

quiz.q: Arjun makes triangles in a row with matchsticks. 1 triangle uses 3 sticks, 2 triangles use 5 sticks, 3 triangles use 7 sticks. How many sticks for 4 triangles?
quiz.explain: Each new triangle shares one stick, so it needs only 2 more sticks. 7 + 2 = 9.
quiz.mistake: Uses 3 new sticks for every triangle (4 × 3 = 12)

quiz.q: A growing pattern has 2 stars, then 4 stars, then 6 stars. How many stars are in the 5th step?
quiz.explain: Each step adds 2 stars: 2, 4, 6, 8, 10. The 5th step has 10.
quiz.mistake: Finds the 4th step instead of the 5th

quiz.q: A rangoli tile turns a quarter turn at each step. How many quarter turns bring it back to how it started?
quiz.explain: 4 quarter turns make one full turn, so the tile is back where it began.
quiz.mistake: Thinks 2 quarter turns make a full turn

quiz.q: Meena's bangles go gold, silver, silver, gold, silver, silver... How many silver bangles are in the first 12?
quiz.explain: Each core of 3 bangles has 2 silver. 12 bangles make 4 cores, so 4 × 2 = 8 silver.
quiz.mistake: Thinks half of the bangles are silver

teach.ask: Gappu has a long bead chain: red, blue, red, blue... How can Gappu know the colour of the 20th bead without counting all of them?
teach.praise: Clever! Find the part that repeats and jump in groups. The 20th bead is blue. Thank you!
teach.nudge: Which small part keeps coming again and again in the chain?

topics.title: Finding the rule of a pattern

learn.hook: Every pattern hides a secret rule. Can you crack the code?
points: To find the rule, look at how you get from one number to the next.
Check the rule on ALL the numbers, not just the first two.
3, 6, 12, 24 looks like 'add 3' at first, but only 'multiply by 2' works for all.
Odd + odd always gives an even number. Even + even always gives an even number.
On a calendar, the date just below any date is 7 more, because a week has 7 days.

example.q: The rule is 'start at 7 and add 3'. What is the 4th number?

learn.reallife: Calendars, times tables and the seats in a cinema hall all follow simple rules.

games.title: Match the pattern to its rule

quiz.q: What is the rule of this pattern? 4, 8, 12, 16
quiz.mistake: Checks only 4 to 8 and thinks it is 'multiply by 2'

quiz.q: The rule is 'start at 7 and add 3'. What is the 4th number?
quiz.explain: 7, 10, 13, 16. The 4th number is 16.
quiz.mistake: Adds 3 four times to 7 and gets the 5th number (19)

quiz.q: Find the missing number: 6, 12, ?, 24, 30
quiz.explain: The rule is add 6. 12 + 6 = 18, and 18 + 6 = 24 checks out.
quiz.mistake: Uses 'add 4' by guessing a smaller jump

quiz.q: Which rule works for ALL the numbers? 3, 6, 12, 24
quiz.explain: 3 × 2 = 6, 6 × 2 = 12, 12 × 2 = 24. 'Add 3' works only for the first step.
quiz.mistake: Checks only the first two numbers

quiz.q: Joseph adds two odd numbers, like 5 + 7 or 3 + 9. What kind of number does he always get?
quiz.explain: Odd + odd is always even. 5 + 7 = 12 and 3 + 9 = 12 are both even.
quiz.mistake: Thinks odd + odd stays odd

quiz.q: What comes next? 1000, 900, 800, ?
quiz.explain: The rule is take away 100. 800 - 100 = 700.
quiz.mistake: Takes away 10 instead of 100

quiz.q: The pattern 11, 22, 33, 44... goes on. What is the 9th number?
quiz.explain: The pattern is the 11 times table. The 9th number is 11 × 9 = 99.
quiz.mistake: Gives the 8th number (88)

quiz.q: On a calendar, which date is just below 5 in the same column?
quiz.explain: Each row of a calendar is one week of 7 days. So the date below is 5 + 7 = 12.
quiz.mistake: Gives the next date (6) which is to the right, not below

teach.ask: Gappu thinks 3, 6, 12, 24 follows the rule 'add 3'. Is Gappu right? How do we check a rule?
teach.praise: Thanks! A rule must work for every number. Here it is 'double it'. Gappu will always check now!
teach.nudge: Does 'add 3' work from 6 to 12? What should Gappu check?

learn.hook: A train can carry more than 1000 people! Let's meet the big 4-digit numbers.
points: 999 + 1 = 1000. It is the smallest 4-digit number. We read it as 'one thousand'.
10 hundreds make 1 thousand. 100 tens also make 1 thousand.
The biggest 4-digit number is 9999.
We read 3405 as 'three thousand four hundred five'. A 0 in a place means nothing is there.
Counting on by 1000 changes only the thousands digit: 2345, 3345, 4345.

example.q: Write 'six thousand eighty' in numerals.

learn.reallife: Prices of bicycles, the number of pages in a big book and people in a stadium are often 4-digit numbers.

games.title: Match the number to its name

quiz.q: What is 999 + 1?
quiz.explain: 999 is the biggest 3-digit number. One more makes 1000, the smallest 4-digit number.
quiz.mistake: Writes the 1 next to 999 instead of adding

quiz.q: How many hundreds make 1 thousand?
quiz.explain: 100 + 100 + ... ten times = 1000. So 10 hundreds make 1 thousand.
quiz.mistake: Confuses 'how many hundreds' with 'how many tens'

quiz.q: Write 'three thousand four hundred five' in numerals.
quiz.explain: 3 thousands, 4 hundreds, 0 tens and 5 ones make 3405.
steps: No tens, so put 0 in the tens place: 3405
quiz.mistake: Forgets the 0 in the tens place, or writes each word as a separate number

quiz.q: How do we read 6080?
quiz.explain: 6080 has 6 thousands, 0 hundreds, 8 tens and 0 ones. That is six thousand eighty.
quiz.mistake: Reads the 8 as hundreds instead of tens

quiz.q: What is 1 more than 4999?
quiz.explain: 4999 + 1 = 5000. All the 9s turn to 0s and the thousands digit goes up by 1.
steps: The carry moves through tens and hundreds
quiz.mistake: Adds 1 to the hundreds place instead of the ones place

quiz.q: What is 100 more than 2950?
quiz.explain: Adding 100 adds 1 to the hundreds. 9 hundreds + 1 hundred = 10 hundreds = 1 thousand. So 2950 becomes 3050.
quiz.mistake: Adds 10 instead of 100, or adds 1000

quiz.q: Arjun counts on by thousands: 2345, 3345, 4345, ? What comes next?
quiz.explain: Each time the thousands digit goes up by 1. 4345 + 1000 = 5345.
quiz.mistake: Adds 10 or 100 instead of 1000

quiz.q: What is the smallest 4-digit number?
quiz.explain: 999 has only 3 digits. The first number with 4 digits is 1000.
quiz.mistake: Picks 999, which is the biggest 3-digit number

teach.ask: Gappu counted 999 grains and then found one more. What number is that, and why is it special?
teach.praise: Hooray! 999 and 1 more is 1000, the first 4-digit number, made of 10 hundreds. Gappu is amazed!
teach.nudge: How many digits does the new number have? How many hundreds are inside it?

learn.hook: In 4725, the 7 is worth 700, not just 7! Where a digit sits decides its value.
points: A 4-digit number has 4 places: thousands, hundreds, tens and ones.
In 4725: 4 thousands, 7 hundreds, 2 tens and 5 ones.
Place value = digit × the value of its place. The 7 in 4725 is worth 7 × 100 = 700.
Expanded form shows each part: 4725 = 4000 + 700 + 20 + 5.
A 0 keeps a place empty: 3047 has 0 hundreds.

example.q: Meena has two ₹1000 notes, five ₹100 notes and three ₹10 notes. How much money is that?

learn.reallife: Shopkeepers count ₹1000, ₹100 and ₹10 notes in bundles, just like thousands, hundreds and tens.

items.text: In 5384, the 3 is worth ___.
In 7062, the 7 is worth ___.
In 1958, the digit in the tens place is ___.
2 thousands and 3 tens = ___

quiz.q: What is the place value of 7 in 4725?
quiz.explain: The 7 is in the hundreds place, so it is worth 7 × 100 = 700.
quiz.mistake: Gives the digit itself (face value) instead of its place value

quiz.q: What number is 5000 + 300 + 20 + 6?
quiz.explain: 5 thousands, 3 hundreds, 2 tens and 6 ones make 5326.
quiz.mistake: Writes the digits in the wrong places

quiz.q: Which digit is in the tens place of 8309?
quiz.explain: 8309 = 8 thousands, 3 hundreds, 0 tens, 9 ones. The tens digit is 0.
quiz.mistake: Reads the places from the left and picks the second digit

quiz.q: What number has 3 thousands, 0 hundreds, 4 tens and 7 ones?
quiz.explain: Write each digit in its place: 3 | 0 | 4 | 7 = 3047.
quiz.mistake: Leaves out the 0 for the hundreds place

quiz.q: Which is the expanded form of 6158?
quiz.explain: 6 thousands = 6000, 1 hundred = 100, 5 tens = 50, 8 ones = 8.
quiz.mistake: Writes the tens digit as ones (5 instead of 50)

quiz.q: Meena has two ₹1000 notes, five ₹100 notes and three ₹10 notes. How much money does she have?
quiz.mistake: Forgets the ₹10 notes, or puts digits in the wrong places

quiz.q: Which number has 9 in the hundreds place?
quiz.explain: In 2934 the places are 2 thousands, 9 hundreds, 3 tens, 4 ones.
quiz.mistake: Picks the number that starts with 9 (that 9 is in the thousands place)

quiz.q: How many tens are there in 1000?
quiz.explain: 10 tens make 100, and 10 hundreds make 1000. So 1000 has 10 × 10 = 100 tens.
quiz.mistake: Thinks there are only 10 tens in a thousand

teach.ask: Gappu says the 7 in 4725 is just worth 7. Is Gappu right? Please explain!
teach.praise: Oh! The 7 is in the hundreds place, so it is worth 700. Place decides value. Thank you!
teach.nudge: Which place is the 7 sitting in? What does that place mean?

learn.hook: Riya's school has 1450 students and Arjun's has 1405. Which school is bigger? Let's compare!
points: A number with more digits is bigger: any 4-digit number is bigger than any 3-digit number.
If both have 4 digits, compare the thousands first. If they are the same, compare the hundreds, then tens, then ones.
We use > for 'greater than', < for 'less than' and = for 'equal to'.
To make the biggest number from some digits, put the biggest digit first. For the smallest, put the smallest digit first (but not 0).

example.q: Which is greater: 4567 or 4657?

learn.reallife: We compare prices of phones, scores in a quiz and heights of mountains using the same steps.

games.title: Greater or smaller?
items: Hundreds are the same (6). Tens: 0 < 2, so 5602 is smaller.
999 has 3 digits and 1000 has 4, so 1000 is bigger.
Both numbers are exactly the same.

quiz.q: Which number is greater: 4567 or 4657?
quiz.explain: The thousands are the same. In the hundreds, 6 > 5, so 4657 is greater.
quiz.mistake: Compares the ones digits first (7 = 7) and gets confused

quiz.q: Which is the largest? 3098, 3890, 3809, 3980
quiz.explain: All have 3 thousands. The hundreds digits are 0, 8, 8, 9. 3980 has 9 hundreds, so it is the largest.
quiz.mistake: Looks at the last digit instead of the first different place

quiz.q: Use the digits 5, 2, 8 and 1 once each. What is the largest 4-digit number you can make?
quiz.explain: Put the digits from biggest to smallest: 8, 5, 2, 1. That makes 8521.
quiz.mistake: Does not put every digit in biggest-to-smallest order

quiz.q: Use the digits 5, 2, 8 and 1 once each. What is the smallest 4-digit number you can make?
quiz.explain: Put the digits from smallest to biggest: 1, 2, 5, 8. That makes 1258.
quiz.mistake: Puts the smallest digit first but mixes up the rest

quiz.q: Which sign goes in the box? 7001 ☐ 7010
quiz.explain: Thousands and hundreds are the same. Tens: 0 < 1, so 7001 < 7010.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a number ending in 1 is bigger than a number ending in 0

quiz.q: Riya's school has 1450 students. Arjun's school has 1405 students. How many more students are in Riya's school?
quiz.mistake: Takes away wrongly and gets 55

quiz.q: Which number comes just before 6000?
quiz.explain: Just before means 1 less. 6000 - 1 = 5999.
quiz.mistake: Takes away 1000 or 100 instead of 1

quiz.q: Which list goes from smallest to largest?
quiz.explain: Compare the hundreds: 0 < 4 = 4 < 5. Then 2405 < 2450 because 0 tens < 5 tens.
quiz.mistake: Compares only the first two digits

teach.ask: Gappu has 5602 seeds and Kabir has 5620. Gappu thinks they have the same. How do we compare?
teach.praise: I see! Start from the thousands, and when digits match, move to the next place. 5620 is bigger!
teach.nudge: Which place should Gappu look at first? What if those digits are the same?

learn.hook: Two friends, one roti. How do you share it so nobody feels cheated? Make equal parts!
points: A fraction is a part of a whole that is cut into EQUAL parts.
1/2 (one half) means 1 of 2 equal parts. 1/4 (one quarter) means 1 of 4 equal parts.
In 3/4, the bottom number (4) tells how many equal parts the whole has. The top number (3) tells how many parts we take.
2 halves make 1 whole. 4 quarters make 1 whole.
The more equal parts you cut a roti into, the smaller each part is. So 1/4 is smaller than 1/2.

example.q: A chikki bar is broken into 3 equal pieces. Meena eats 2 pieces. What fraction did she eat?
steps: The whole has 3 equal pieces, so the bottom number is 3.
She ate 2 pieces, so the top number is 2.

learn.reallife: We share pizza slices, cut oranges into pieces and fold paper into halves for craft.

games.title: Match the words to the fraction
Equal parts?
items: A cake cut into 2 pieces, one big and one small, shows halves.
1/4 of a roti is bigger than 1/2 of the same roti.
Cutting into 4 parts makes smaller pieces than cutting into 2.
In 3/5, the whole has 5 equal parts.
The bottom number tells how many equal parts make the whole.

quiz.q: A roti is cut into 4 equal parts. Arjun eats 1 part. What fraction of the roti did he eat?
quiz.explain: The roti has 4 equal parts and Arjun ate 1 of them. That is 1/4.
quiz.mistake: Writes the numbers upside down (4/1)

quiz.q: A chikki bar is broken into 3 equal pieces. Meena eats 2 of them. What fraction did she eat?
quiz.explain: There are 3 equal pieces and she ate 2. So she ate 2/3.
quiz.mistake: Gives the part left over (1/3) instead of the part eaten

quiz.q: How many halves make one whole?
quiz.explain: A half is 1 of 2 equal parts. Two halves together make the whole.
quiz.mistake: Thinks one half is already a whole

quiz.q: Which of these shows halves?
options: A cake cut into one big piece and one small piece
A paper folded into 2 parts that match exactly
An orange cut into 3 equal pieces
A roti torn into 2 pieces of any size
quiz.explain: Halves are 2 EQUAL parts. Only the paper folded so the parts match exactly shows halves.
quiz.mistake: Thinks any 2 pieces are halves, even if they are not equal

quiz.q: A ribbon is cut into 8 equal pieces. Kabir uses 3 pieces. What fraction of the ribbon is left?
quiz.explain: 8 - 3 = 5 pieces are left out of 8. That is 5/8.
quiz.mistake: Gives the fraction used (3/8) instead of the fraction left

quiz.q: Which is bigger: 1/2 of a roti or 1/4 of the same roti?
quiz.explain: Cutting into 2 equal parts gives bigger pieces than cutting into 4. So 1/2 is bigger.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a bigger bottom number means a bigger fraction

quiz.q: What does the fraction 3/4 mean?
quiz.explain: The whole is cut into 4 equal parts and we take 3 of them.
quiz.mistake: Forgets that the parts must be equal

quiz.q: A watermelon is cut into 6 equal slices. Aisha and her brother eat 1 slice each. What fraction of the watermelon did they eat?
quiz.explain: They ate 1 + 1 = 2 slices out of 6 equal slices. That is 2/6.
quiz.mistake: Counts only one person's slice

teach.ask: Gappu broke a biscuit into 2 pieces, one big and one tiny, and called each piece a half. Is that right?
teach.praise: Got it! Halves must be 2 equal parts. Gappu will break the next biscuit fairly!
teach.nudge: Were Gappu's two pieces the same size? Does that matter?

topics.title: Sharing a group: fractions of a collection

learn.hook: Dadi has 12 laddoos and says half are for you. How many is that? Let's share!
points: To find a fraction of a group, first make equal groups.
Half of 12: make 2 equal groups. Each group has 12 ÷ 2 = 6.
One quarter of 20: make 4 equal groups. Each group has 20 ÷ 4 = 5.
To find 3/4 of 16, find 1/4 first (16 ÷ 4 = 4), then take 3 groups: 3 × 4 = 12.
The bottom number tells how many groups to make. The top number tells how many groups to take.

example.q: Harpreet has 18 pencils. She gives 1/3 of them to Joseph. How many does she give, and how many are left?
steps: 1/3 is one group: she gives 6 pencils.

learn.reallife: Sharing sweets on Diwali, dividing marbles among friends or splitting a bill all use fractions of a group.

items.text: Half of 10 bangles is ___ bangles.
1/4 of 16 marbles is ___ marbles.
To find 1/3 of a group, make ___ equal groups.
3/4 of 20 kites is ___ kites.

quiz.q: Dadi has 12 laddoos. She gives half of them to Riya. How many laddoos does Riya get?
quiz.explain: Half means 2 equal groups. 12 ÷ 2 = 6.
quiz.mistake: Takes away 2 instead of dividing by 2

quiz.q: What is one quarter of 20 marbles?
quiz.explain: A quarter means 4 equal groups. 20 ÷ 4 = 5.
quiz.mistake: Gives the number of groups (4) instead of the number in each group

quiz.q: What is 1/3 of 15 mangoes?
quiz.explain: Make 3 equal groups. 15 ÷ 3 = 5 in each group.
quiz.mistake: Takes away 3 from 15

quiz.q: What is 3/4 of 16 diyas?
quiz.explain: 1/4 of 16 is 4. 3/4 is three of those groups: 3 × 4 = 12.
quiz.mistake: Finds only 1/4 and stops

quiz.q: Harpreet has 18 pencils. She gives 1/3 of them to Joseph. How many pencils does Harpreet have left?
quiz.explain: 1/3 of 18 is 6, which she gives away. 18 - 6 = 12 are left.
quiz.mistake: Gives the part given away instead of the part left

quiz.q: Kabir has ₹40. He spends 1/4 of it on a kite. How much does the kite cost?
quiz.mistake: Finds half (₹20) instead of a quarter

quiz.q: What is 2/5 of 25 laddoos?
quiz.mistake: Finds 1/5 only

quiz.q: Joseph shares 24 grapes equally among 4 friends. What fraction of the grapes does each friend get?
quiz.explain: Each friend gets 1 of 4 equal shares, so each gets 1/4 of the grapes. (That is 6 grapes.)
quiz.mistake: Gives the number of grapes (6) instead of the fraction

teach.ask: Gappu has 20 seeds and wants to give 1/4 of them to a friend. How many seeds should Gappu give?
teach.praise: Yes! Make 4 equal groups and give 1 group: 5 seeds. Gappu's friend is happy!
teach.nudge: How many equal groups should Gappu make for a quarter?

learn.hook: Mummy asks for 'half a kilo of tomatoes' and 'a quarter litre of milk'. Fractions help us measure!
points: 1 metre = 100 cm, so 1/2 metre = 50 cm and 1/4 metre = 25 cm.
1 kilogram = 1000 g, so 1/2 kg = 500 g and 1/4 kg = 250 g.
1 litre = 1000 ml, so 1/2 litre = 500 ml and 3/4 litre = 750 ml.
1 hour = 60 minutes, so half an hour = 30 minutes and a quarter of an hour = 15 minutes.
To find 3/4 of a measure, find 1/4 first, then multiply by 3.

example.q: How many centimetres is 3/4 of a metre?

learn.reallife: Shopkeepers sell ½ kg of sugar, milkmen pour ½ litre, and tailors cut ¼ metre of lace.

games.title: Match the fraction to the measure

quiz.q: How many centimetres are there in half a metre?
quiz.explain: 1 metre = 100 cm. Half of 100 cm is 50 cm.
quiz.mistake: Uses 1000 instead of 100 for a metre, or finds a quarter

quiz.q: How many grams is 1/4 kg?
quiz.mistake: Uses 100 g for a kilogram (gets 25 g)

quiz.q: Aisha buys 1/2 litre of milk. How many millilitres is that?
quiz.explain: 1 litre = 1000 ml. Half of 1000 ml is 500 ml.
quiz.mistake: Uses 100 ml for a litre

quiz.q: How many minutes are there in a quarter of an hour?
quiz.explain: 1 hour = 60 minutes. 60 ÷ 4 = 15 minutes.
quiz.mistake: Thinks an hour has 100 minutes (gets 25)

quiz.q: How many centimetres is 3/4 of a metre?
quiz.mistake: Writes the digits 3 and 4 together (34)

quiz.q: Meena buys 2 packets of sugar. Each packet is 1/2 kg. How much sugar is that?
quiz.explain: Two halves make one whole. 1/2 kg + 1/2 kg = 1 kg.
quiz.mistake: Counts the packets (2) as kilograms

quiz.q: Which is heavier: 1/2 kg of rice or 300 g of dal?
quiz.explain: 1/2 kg = 500 g, and 500 g is more than 300 g. So the rice is heavier.
quiz.mistake: Sees 300 is bigger than 1/2 and forgets to change kg to g

quiz.q: Joseph has a 1 m ribbon. He cuts it into 4 equal pieces. How long is each piece?
quiz.explain: Each piece is 1/4 of a metre. 100 cm ÷ 4 = 25 cm.
quiz.mistake: Gives the number of pieces as the length

teach.ask: The shopkeeper gave Gappu 500 g of peanuts when Gappu asked for half a kilo. Was Gappu cheated?
teach.praise: Phew! 1 kg is 1000 g, and half of 1000 is 500. The shopkeeper was fair. Thank you!
teach.nudge: How many grams are there in 1 kg? What is half of that?

learn.hook: Is your classroom door taller than your dad? Metres and centimetres can tell!
points: We measure short lengths, like a pencil, in centimetres (cm).
We measure longer lengths, like a room or a rope, in metres (m).
1 metre = 100 centimetres.
To change metres to centimetres, multiply by 100: 3 m = 300 cm.
1 m 30 cm means 100 cm + 30 cm = 130 cm.

example.q: Riya is 1 m 30 cm tall. What is her height in centimetres?

learn.reallife: A tailor measures you in centimetres. A cloth shop sells cloth by the metre.

quiz.q: How many centimetres make 1 metre?
quiz.explain: 1 metre is the same as 100 centimetres.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up metres with kilograms (1000) or with minutes (60)

quiz.q: Which unit is best to measure the length of a pencil?
quiz.explain: A pencil is short, so we use centimetres. Kilogram measures weight and litre measures liquid.
quiz.mistake: Picks a unit that does not measure length

quiz.q: How many centimetres are there in 3 m?
quiz.explain: Each metre is 100 cm. 3 × 100 = 300 cm.
quiz.mistake: Multiplies by 10 instead of 100

quiz.q: Which rope is longer: one that is 1 m long or one that is 90 cm long?
quiz.explain: 1 m = 100 cm, and 100 cm is more than 90 cm.
quiz.mistake: Thinks 90 is bigger than 1 without changing the units

quiz.q: A cloth piece is 400 cm long. How many metres is that?
quiz.explain: 100 cm make 1 m, so 400 cm make 400 ÷ 100 = 4 m.
quiz.mistake: Divides by 10 instead of 100

quiz.q: Kabir's ruler is 30 cm long. How many such rulers placed end to end make exactly 3 m?
quiz.mistake: Forgets to change 3 m into 300 cm

quiz.q: Riya is 1 m 30 cm tall. What is her height in centimetres?
quiz.mistake: Writes 1 and 30 side by side, or writes 1 m as 1000 cm

quiz.q: Which length is the longest?
quiz.explain: Change all to cm: 2 m = 200 cm, 199 cm, 250 cm, 1 m 90 cm = 190 cm. 250 cm is the longest.
quiz.mistake: Compares numbers without changing them to the same unit

teach.ask: Gappu measured a rope: 2 m. Kabir says it is 200 cm. Who is right?
teach.praise: Both are right! 1 m is 100 cm, so 2 m is 200 cm. Gappu is happy!
teach.nudge: How many centimetres are in one metre? Can two answers both be correct?

learn.hook: Diwali lights, garlands and ribbons: how much do we need altogether? Let's add lengths!
points: To add or subtract lengths, first make the units the same.
If you get 100 cm or more, change 100 cm into 1 m: 125 cm = 1 m 25 cm.
To find how much longer, subtract the shorter length from the longer one.
To find how much is left after cutting, subtract the cut part.

example.q: Meena has a 75 cm ribbon and a 50 cm ribbon. What is their total length in m and cm?

learn.reallife: When you decorate for Diwali, you add up the lengths of light strings to see if they will cover the balcony.

quiz.q: Meena's plait is 45 cm long. How much shorter is it than 1 m?
quiz.mistake: Makes a mistake taking away from 100, or adds instead

quiz.q: Riya has a 3 m rope. She cuts off 120 cm for a swing. How much rope is left?
quiz.mistake: Takes 3 away from 120 without changing metres to cm

quiz.q: Kabir runs 5 rounds of a 100 m track. How far does he run?
quiz.explain: 5 rounds of 100 m is 5 × 100 = 500 m.
quiz.mistake: Adds 5 to 100 instead of multiplying

quiz.q: Arjun is 1 m 32 cm tall. His sister is 1 m 18 cm tall. How much taller is Arjun?
steps: 1 m 32 cm = 132 cm, 1 m 18 cm = 118 cm
quiz.mistake: Adds the heights or takes away wrongly

quiz.q: Aisha joins 4 garland pieces, each 60 cm long. What is the total length?
quiz.mistake: Writes 240 cm as 240 m, or adds 4 + 60

quiz.q: Joseph's desk is 1 m long. How many 25 cm long books fit end to end along it?
quiz.mistake: Takes away 25 from 100 instead of dividing

quiz.q: Harpreet walks 650 m to school and then 650 m back home. How far does she walk in all?
quiz.mistake: Counts only one way

quiz.q: Meena has a 75 cm ribbon and a 50 cm ribbon. What is their total length?
quiz.mistake: Writes 125 cm as 125 m

teach.ask: Gappu has a 2 m string and a 50 cm string. Gappu says together they are 52. Is that right?
teach.praise: Thank you! Change 2 m to 200 cm first, then add: 250 cm, which is 2 m 50 cm!
teach.nudge: Are metres and centimetres the same unit? What should Gappu do first?

learn.hook: No ruler? No problem! Your hand and feet can help you guess lengths.
points: To estimate means to make a smart guess, close to the real answer.
Use body measures: a handspan is about 15 cm, a big step is about 50 cm for a child.
A door is about 2 m tall. A cricket pitch is about 20 m long. An eraser is about 4 cm long.
Check your guess by measuring. A good estimate is close to the real length.

example.q: Riya's handspan is about 15 cm. Her table is 6 handspans long. About how long is the table?

learn.reallife: Before buying a mat, you can step across the room to guess if it will fit.

games.title: Good estimate?
items: A classroom door is about 2 m tall.
That is a little taller than most grown-ups.
A pencil is about 2 m long.
A pencil is about 15 to 20 cm long.
An eraser is about 4 cm long.
It fits easily in your hand.
A school bus is about 50 cm long.
A bus is many metres long.
A cricket bat is closer to 1 m than to 1 cm.
A cricket bat is a bit less than 1 m long.
A grain of rice is about 1 m long.
It is only a few millimetres, much less than 1 cm.

quiz.q: What is the best estimate for the height of a classroom door?
quiz.explain: A door is a little taller than a grown-up, which is about 2 m.
quiz.mistake: Picks the right number with the wrong unit

quiz.q: What is the best estimate for the length of an eraser?
quiz.explain: An eraser fits in your palm, so it is only a few centimetres long.
quiz.mistake: Does not picture how big a metre is

quiz.q: Riya's handspan is about 15 cm. Her table is 6 handspans long. About how long is the table?
quiz.explain: 6 handspans of 15 cm each is 6 × 15 = 90 cm.
quiz.mistake: Adds 6 + 15 instead of multiplying

quiz.q: Arjun's step is about 50 cm long. About how many steps will he take to walk 5 m?
quiz.mistake: Forgets to change metres to centimetres

quiz.q: Which of these is closest to 1 m long?
quiz.explain: A cricket bat is a little less than 1 m long. The others are much smaller or much bigger.
quiz.mistake: Does not have a picture of 1 m in mind

quiz.q: Kabir guessed that his book was 40 cm long. He measured it and it was 32 cm. How far off was his guess?
quiz.explain: 40 - 32 = 8 cm. His guess was 8 cm too long.
quiz.mistake: Adds the two lengths instead of finding the difference

quiz.q: Which of these would you measure in metres?
quiz.explain: A cricket pitch is long, about 20 m. The others are small and are measured in cm or smaller.
quiz.mistake: Thinks metres are used for small things

quiz.q: A cricket pitch is about 20 m long. Meena walks along it 3 times. About how far does she walk?
quiz.mistake: Adds 3 instead of multiplying by 3

teach.ask: Gappu has no ruler but wants to know how long the bench is. What can Gappu do?
teach.praise: Smart! Use handspans or steps to estimate, then check with a ruler later. Gappu tried it!
teach.nudge: What could Gappu use from Gappu's own body to guess the length?

learn.hook: A village collected 1250 kg of plastic in March and 1475 kg in April. What a clean-up! How much in all?
points: Write the numbers one below the other: ones under ones, tens under tens, and so on.
Start adding from the ones place, then tens, hundreds and thousands.
If a place adds up to 10 or more, write the ones digit and carry 1 to the next place.
Check your answer by estimating: 1250 + 1475 is about 1300 + 1500 = 2800, so 2725 makes sense.
learn.reallife: Village panchayats add up the waste collected each month to see how clean the village is getting.

quiz.explain: No carrying is needed. 5 + 4 = 9, 4 + 3 = 7, 3 + 2 = 5, 2 + 1 = 3. So 3579.
quiz.mistake: Takes away instead of adding (gets 1111)
Forgets to add the carried 1

quiz.q: The village collected 1250 kg of plastic in March and 1475 kg in April. How much plastic is that altogether?
quiz.mistake: Forgets to carry from the tens place
Forgets the carry into the thousands place

quiz.q: Find the missing number: ___ + 2500 = 6000
quiz.explain: The missing number is 6000 - 2500 = 3500. Check: 3500 + 2500 = 6000.
quiz.mistake: Adds 2500 to 6000 instead of finding the difference

quiz.explain: 2000 + 2000 = 4000. We added 1 extra twice, so take away 2: 3998.
quiz.mistake: Rounds both numbers to 2000 and forgets to take back the extra

quiz.q: Three wards cleaned 1200 m, 350 m and 45 m of drains. How many metres in all?
quiz.mistake: Lines up the numbers from the left instead of the right

quiz.q: About how much is 2980 + 4030? Choose the best estimate.
quiz.mistake: Rounds one number the wrong way

teach.ask: Gappu added 4678 + 2516 and got 6184. What did Gappu forget?
teach.praise: Oh! When a place makes 10 or more, Gappu must carry 1 to the next place. The answer is 7194!
teach.nudge: What happens when 8 + 6 makes 14? Where does the extra ten go?

learn.hook: The village had 4500 trees. 1250 were planted this year. How many are old? Subtraction to the rescue!
points: Write the bigger number on top. Line up ones, tens, hundreds and thousands.
Start from the ones place. If the top digit is smaller, borrow 1 from the next place (it becomes 10 here).
With zeros, like 6000 - 2475, borrow across: 6000 becomes 5 thousands, 9 hundreds, 9 tens and 10 ones.
Check subtraction by adding: answer + number taken away = the starting number.

example.q: Subtract 7302 - 4568.
steps: Tens: 0 became 9 after borrowing from hundreds. 9 - 6 = 3.

learn.reallife: Shopkeepers subtract to give change, and the gram sabha subtracts to see how much money is left for cleaning tools.

games.title: Check by adding
items: Adding back gives the starting number, so it is correct.
In 7302 - 4568, we must borrow in the ones place.
2 is less than 8, so we borrow.
When we borrow, the top digit gets 100 more.
It gets 10 more, because 1 from the next place is 10 here.

quiz.explain: No borrowing is needed: 8 - 5 = 3, 7 - 4 = 3, 6 - 3 = 3, 5 - 2 = 3.
quiz.mistake: Adds instead of subtracting (8023)

quiz.explain: Borrow across the zeros: 6000 is 5 thousands, 9 hundreds, 9 tens and 10 ones. 10 - 5 = 5, 9 - 7 = 2, 9 - 4 = 5, 5 - 2 = 3. So 3525.
quiz.mistake: Forgets that borrowing makes the thousands digit 1 less
Takes the smaller digit from the bigger one in every place (gets 3266)

quiz.q: The village has 4500 trees. 1250 of them were planted this year. How many trees are older?
quiz.mistake: Adds the numbers instead of subtracting

quiz.q: Find the missing number: 8000 - ___ = 3200
quiz.explain: The missing number is 8000 - 3200 = 4800. Check: 8000 - 4800 = 3200.

quiz.q: Riya worked out 5420 - 1385 = 4035. To check, she adds 4035 + 1385. What should she get?
quiz.explain: If the subtraction is right, adding back gives the start number. 4035 + 1385 = 5420.
quiz.mistake: Does not know that addition undoes subtraction

quiz.q: How much more is 9000 than 6750?
quiz.mistake: Makes a borrowing mistake and gets 3250

quiz.q: Meena had ₹2000. She spent ₹1345 on cleaning brooms and buckets. How much money is left?
quiz.mistake: Forgets to reduce digits after borrowing across zeros

teach.ask: Gappu tried 6000 - 2475 but cannot take 5 from 0. What should Gappu do?
teach.praise: Yes! Borrow across the zeros, subtract, and add back to check. Gappu got 3525!
teach.nudge: When the top digit is 0, where can Gappu get some more from?

learn.hook: A good problem-solver first asks: should I add or subtract? Let's learn the clue words!
points: Read the problem twice. Find what is given and what is asked.
Words like 'altogether', 'in all' and 'total' usually mean add.
Words like 'how many more', 'how many left' and 'difference' usually mean subtract.
Some problems have two steps. Do one step at a time.
Check if your answer makes sense.

example.q: A village had 2500 plants. The children planted 1200 more, but 300 dried up. How many plants are there now?

learn.reallife: Swachh Bharat drives count how many bags were filled and how many are still left to fill.

items.text: 1235 children and 1180 children march in a rally. In all, ___ children march.
A train has 1200 seats. 875 are booked. ___ seats are empty.
The goal is 6000 kg. 4800 kg is done. ___ kg more is needed.

quiz.q: Green village has 1345 people and Blue village has 2678 people. How many people live in both villages?
quiz.explain: 'Both villages' means add. 1345 + 2678 = 4023.
quiz.mistake: Forgets one of the carries

quiz.q: Children collected 3250 bottles. 1875 have been sent for recycling. How many are not yet sent?
quiz.explain: 'Not yet sent' means what is left. 3250 - 1875 = 1375.
quiz.mistake: Adds the numbers instead of subtracting

quiz.q: 'How many more' in a word problem usually tells you to do what?
quiz.explain: 'How many more' asks for the difference between two numbers, so we subtract.
quiz.mistake: Sees the word 'more' and thinks it means add

quiz.q: A village had 2500 plants. Children planted 1200 more, but 300 dried up. How many plants are there now?
quiz.mistake: Does only the first step, or adds the 300 too

quiz.q: The compost pit made 1450 kg of compost in Week 1 and 1650 kg in Week 2. How much more was made in Week 2?
quiz.mistake: Adds both weeks instead of finding the difference

quiz.q: A train has 1200 seats. 875 seats are booked. How many seats are still empty?
quiz.explain: 1200 - 875 = 325 empty seats.
quiz.mistake: Makes a borrowing mistake and gets 425

quiz.q: Aisha's village wants to collect 6000 kg of waste for recycling. It has collected 4800 kg. How much more is needed?
quiz.mistake: Adds the goal and what is collected

quiz.q: School A sent 1235 children and School B sent 1180 children to a cleanliness rally. How many children joined in all?
quiz.explain: 'In all' means add. 1235 + 1180 = 2415.
quiz.mistake: Forgets the carry from the tens, or subtracts

teach.ask: Gappu reads a story sum but doesn't know whether to add or subtract. Which words give a clue?
teach.praise: Thank you! 'In all' means add and 'how many left' means subtract. Gappu can solve story sums now!
teach.nudge: Which words tell Gappu to add? Which words tell Gappu to take away?

learn.hook: Which is heavier: a kilo of cotton or a kilo of iron? Think before you answer!
points: We measure how heavy things are in grams (g) and kilograms (kg).
1 kilogram = 1000 grams.
Light things like a biscuit packet or a pencil are weighed in grams. Heavy things like a sack of rice or a person are weighed in kilograms.
1 kg of anything weighs the same as 1 kg of anything else.

example.q: A watermelon balances three 1 kg weights and one 500 g weight. How heavy is it in grams?

learn.reallife: At the sabzi mandi, the shopkeeper puts weights of 1 kg, 500 g and 250 g on the balance.

quiz.q: How many grams make 1 kilogram?
quiz.explain: 1 kilogram is the same as 1000 grams.
quiz.mistake: Thinks 1 kg is 100 g, like 1 m is 100 cm

quiz.q: How many grams are there in 3 kg?
quiz.explain: Each kilogram is 1000 g. 3 × 1000 = 3000 g.
quiz.mistake: Multiplies by 100 instead of 1000

quiz.q: Which unit is best for weighing a packet of biscuits?
quiz.explain: A biscuit packet is light, so grams are best. Litres are for liquids and metres are for length.
quiz.mistake: Picks a unit that measures something else

quiz.q: Which is heavier: 1 kg of cotton or 1 kg of iron?
quiz.explain: Both weigh exactly 1 kg. The cotton just takes up much more space.
quiz.mistake: Thinks iron is always heavier because it feels hard

quiz.q: How many grams is 2 kg 500 g?
quiz.mistake: Writes 2 and 500 with a 0 in between

quiz.q: A bag of potatoes weighs 4000 g. How many kilograms is that?
quiz.mistake: Divides by 100 or 10 instead of 1000

quiz.q: Joseph puts weights of 500 g, 250 g and 250 g on a balance. What is the total weight?
quiz.mistake: Adds only two of the weights

quiz.q: A watermelon balances three 1 kg weights and one 500 g weight. How heavy is the watermelon?
quiz.mistake: Writes 3 and 5 together without thinking of place value

teach.ask: Gappu's bag says 1500 g and Kabir's says 1 kg 500 g. Whose bag is heavier?
teach.praise: Wow! 1 kg is 1000 g, so 1 kg 500 g is 1500 g. They weigh the same!
teach.nudge: How many grams are there in 1 kg? Try changing Kabir's weight to grams.

learn.hook: How many glasses of nimbu paani can you pour from one big jug? Let's find out!
points: Capacity is how much liquid a container can hold.
We measure capacity in millilitres (ml) and litres (l).
1 litre = 1000 millilitres.
Small amounts like a spoon of medicine are in ml. Big amounts like a bucket of water are in litres.
2 l 250 ml means 2000 ml + 250 ml = 2250 ml.

example.q: A jug holds 1 l of nimbu paani. How many 250 ml glasses can it fill?

learn.reallife: Milk packets come in 500 ml and 1 l. Water bottles are often 1 l. Medicine is measured in ml with a small cup.

games.title: True or false?
items: That is the rule for capacity.
A bucket of water is best measured in millilitres.
A bucket holds a lot, so we use litres.
Two 500 ml bottles hold 1 litre in all.
A spoon of medicine is about 5 litres.
A spoon holds only about 5 ml.
2 l 500 ml is the same as 2500 ml.
A 250 ml glass holds more than a 1 l jug.
1 l = 1000 ml, which is more than 250 ml.

quiz.q: How many millilitres make 1 litre?
quiz.explain: 1 litre is the same as 1000 millilitres.
quiz.mistake: Thinks 1 l is 100 ml

quiz.q: Which unit is best to measure the water in a bucket?
quiz.explain: A bucket holds a lot of water, so litres are best.
quiz.mistake: Picks millilitres for a big amount

quiz.q: Which unit is best to measure one spoon of cough syrup?
quiz.explain: A spoon holds only a little liquid, so we use millilitres.
quiz.mistake: Picks litres for a tiny amount

quiz.q: How many millilitres is 2 l 250 ml?
quiz.mistake: Puts the digits in the wrong places

quiz.q: A jug holds 1 l of nimbu paani. How many 250 ml glasses can it fill?
quiz.mistake: Forgets that 1 l is 1000 ml

quiz.q: A tank has 3000 ml of water. How many litres is that?
quiz.mistake: Divides by 100 instead of 1000

quiz.q: Riya drinks 200 ml of milk every day. How much milk does she drink in 5 days?
quiz.explain: 5 × 200 ml = 1000 ml, which is 1 litre.
quiz.mistake: Adds 200 + 5 or multiplies wrongly

quiz.q: A bottle holds 500 ml. Arjun has poured in 350 ml. How much more water is needed to fill it?
quiz.mistake: Adds the amounts instead of subtracting

teach.ask: Gappu has a 1 litre jug and some 250 ml cups. How many cups can Gappu fill?
teach.praise: Yes! 1 litre is 1000 ml, and 1000 ÷ 250 is 4 cups. Gappu is pouring now!
teach.nudge: How many millilitres are in 1 litre? How many 250s fit in it?

learn.hook: Mummy's shopping bag is getting heavy! Let's add, subtract and share weights and liquids.
points: To add or subtract, first write both amounts in the same unit, like grams or millilitres.
Add kg with kg and g with g. If the grams make 1000 or more, change 1000 g into 1 kg.
To share equally, divide.
To compare, change both to the same unit first.

example.q: Mummy buys 2 kg 500 g of potatoes and 1 kg 750 g of onions. What is the total weight?

learn.reallife: Cooks measure flour and milk for recipes, and shopkeepers add weights to make a bill.

items.text: A 5 kg rice bag minus 1200 g leaves ___ g.
Each laddoo weighs 50 g. 1 kg has ___ laddoos.
1500 ml shared equally in 3 glasses gives ___ ml each.

quiz.q: Mummy buys 2 kg 500 g of potatoes and 1 kg 750 g of onions. What is the total weight?
quiz.mistake: Adds the grams but does not change 1000 g into 1 kg

quiz.q: A bag holds 5 kg of rice. 1200 g is used for a family function. How much rice is left?
quiz.mistake: Forgets to change kg into g before subtracting

quiz.q: A tank has 10 l of water. Kabir takes out 2 l in a bucket, 3 times. How much water is left?
quiz.explain: He takes out 3 × 2 = 6 l. 10 - 6 = 4 l are left.
quiz.mistake: Takes out the bucket only once

quiz.q: Kabir weighs 32 kg and Aisha weighs 28 kg. What is their total weight?
quiz.mistake: Finds the difference instead of the total

quiz.q: Each laddoo weighs 50 g. How many laddoos make 1 kg?
quiz.mistake: Uses 100 g for 1 kg

quiz.q: A jug has 1 l 500 ml of juice. It is poured equally into 3 glasses. How much juice is in each glass?
quiz.mistake: Forgets to change 1 l into 1000 ml

quiz.q: Which holds more: 2 bottles of 750 ml each, or 1 bottle of 1 l 250 ml?
quiz.mistake: Compares 750 with 1250 and forgets there are 2 bottles

quiz.q: Harpreet's school bag weighs 3 kg. She adds a 750 g lunch box. What does the bag weigh now, in grams?
quiz.mistake: Adds 3 + 750 without changing kg into g

teach.ask: Gappu added 2 kg and 300 g and got 302 g. What went wrong?
teach.praise: I see! First change 2 kg into 2000 g, then add 300 g. That makes 2300 g!
teach.nudge: Can Gappu add kilograms and grams directly? What should Gappu change first?

learn.hook: 4 plates with 6 laddoos on each. Count one by one? No way! Multiply!
points: Multiplication is a quick way to add equal groups.
An array is objects in rows and columns. 3 rows of 7 = 3 × 7 = 21.
Order does not change the answer: 6 × 4 = 4 × 6.
Any number × 1 = the same number. Any number × 0 = 0.

example.q: A rangoli has 3 rows of diyas with 7 diyas in each row. How many diyas are there?

learn.reallife: Eggs in trays, chairs in rows and seats in a train coach are all equal groups.

quiz.q: There are 4 plates with 6 laddoos on each plate. How many laddoos are there?
quiz.explain: 4 groups of 6 is 6 + 6 + 6 + 6 = 24. That is 4 × 6.
quiz.mistake: Adds 4 + 6 instead of multiplying

quiz.q: A rangoli has 3 rows of diyas with 7 diyas in each row. How many diyas are there?
quiz.explain: 3 rows of 7 is 3 × 7 = 21.
quiz.mistake: Adds the rows and the diyas in a row

quiz.q: What is 8 × 7?
quiz.explain: 8 × 7 = 56. You can think 8 × 7 = 7 × 8.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up 8 × 7 with 9 × 7 or 6 × 9

quiz.q: Which is the same as 5 + 5 + 5 + 5 + 5 + 5?
quiz.explain: There are 6 fives, so it is 6 × 5 = 30.
quiz.mistake: Miscounts how many fives are added

quiz.q: What is 9 × 6?
quiz.mistake: Mixes up 9 × 6 with 9 × 5

quiz.q: Each auto-rickshaw carries 3 children to school. How many children do 9 autos carry?
quiz.explain: 9 groups of 3 = 9 × 3 = 27.
quiz.mistake: Adds 9 + 3

quiz.q: What is 0 × 845?
quiz.explain: Zero groups of anything is nothing. Any number × 0 = 0.
quiz.mistake: Thinks multiplying by 0 leaves the number the same

quiz.explain: Changing the order does not change the answer. 6 × 4 = 4 × 6 = 24.
quiz.mistake: Writes the answer 24 instead of the missing number

teach.ask: Gappu has 5 baskets with 4 mangoes in each. Gappu is counting one by one. Is there a faster way?
teach.praise: Yes! 5 equal groups of 4 is 5 × 4 = 20. Multiplying is so fast!
teach.nudge: Are the baskets equal? What can Gappu do with equal groups?

learn.hook: A bus has 48 seats. How many seats in 4 buses? Let's multiply big numbers!
points: Break the bigger number into tens and ones: 23 = 20 + 3.
Multiply each part and add: 23 × 3 = 20 × 3 + 3 × 3 = 60 + 9 = 69.
In column method, multiply the ones first. If you get 10 or more, carry to the tens.
To multiply by 10, put a 0 at the end: 34 × 10 = 340.

example.q: Find 17 × 6.

learn.reallife: A school counts how many students fit in 4 buses, or how many diyas are needed for 8 rows of 15.

quiz.q: What is 23 × 3?
quiz.mistake: Adds 23 + 3 instead of multiplying

quiz.q: What is 45 × 2?
quiz.mistake: Forgets to multiply the ones part

quiz.q: What is 34 × 10?
quiz.explain: Multiplying by 10 puts a 0 at the end. 34 × 10 = 340.
quiz.mistake: Adds 10 instead of multiplying by 10

quiz.q: What is 17 × 6?
quiz.mistake: Forgets to add the carried 4 (gets 62)

quiz.q: A school bus has 48 seats. How many seats are there in 4 such buses?
quiz.mistake: Forgets to carry the 3 from 32 (gets 162)

quiz.q: What is 25 × 4?
quiz.mistake: Multiplies only the tens (gets 80)

quiz.q: What is 125 × 3?
quiz.mistake: Forgets to carry the 1 from 15

quiz.q: For Diwali, Kabir makes 8 rows of diyas with 15 diyas in each row. How many diyas is that?
quiz.mistake: Multiplies only the 10 part (gets 80)

teach.ask: Gappu wants to find 24 × 3 but only knows small tables. How can Gappu do it?
teach.praise: Brilliant! 20 × 3 = 60 and 4 × 3 = 12, so 60 + 12 = 72. Gappu can multiply big numbers now!
teach.nudge: Can Gappu break 24 into smaller, easier parts first?

learn.hook: 20 laddoos, 4 friends. How many each so nobody fights? Division shares fairly!
points: Division means sharing equally or making equal groups.
20 ÷ 4 = 5 means 20 shared among 4 gives 5 each.
Division is the opposite of multiplication. If 6 × 9 = 54, then 54 ÷ 9 = 6 and 54 ÷ 6 = 9.
Sometimes things are left over. This is the remainder. 17 shared among 5 gives 3 each and 2 left over.

example.q: 48 pencils are packed in boxes of 6. How many boxes are needed?

learn.reallife: Sharing sweets, putting children into teams and packing things in boxes all use division.

quiz.q: 20 laddoos are shared equally among 4 friends. How many does each friend get?
quiz.mistake: Takes away 4 instead of dividing

quiz.q: What is 18 ÷ 3?
quiz.mistake: Halves 18 instead of dividing by 3

quiz.q: 35 marbles are put in groups of 7. How many groups are there?
quiz.mistake: Gives the size of each group instead of the number of groups

quiz.q: What is 56 ÷ 8?
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the 8 times table

quiz.q: If 6 × 9 = 54, what is 54 ÷ 9?
quiz.explain: Division undoes multiplication. 6 × 9 = 54, so 54 ÷ 9 = 6.
quiz.mistake: Does not see how multiplication and division are linked

quiz.q: 17 bananas are shared equally among 5 monkeys. How many bananas are left over?
quiz.explain: Each monkey gets 3 bananas (5 × 3 = 15). 17 - 15 = 2 are left over.
quiz.mistake: Gives the number each monkey gets (3) instead of the remainder

quiz.q: 48 pencils are packed in boxes of 6. How many boxes are needed?
quiz.mistake: Takes away 6 from 48 instead of dividing

quiz.q: Kabir reads 63 pages of a story book in 7 days. He reads the same number of pages each day. How many pages does he read daily?
quiz.mistake: Mixes up 7 × 8 and 7 × 9

teach.ask: Gappu has 12 berries and 3 friends. How can Gappu share them fairly?
teach.praise: Thank you! 12 ÷ 3 = 4 each, because 3 × 4 = 12. Everyone is happy!
teach.nudge: How many berries should each friend get so it is fair? Which times table helps?

learn.hook: Forest rangers count animals, trees and visitors. Their numbers get really big! Let's solve their problems.
points: Read the problem slowly. Write down the numbers you are given.
Decide what is asked: a total (add) or a difference (subtract)?
Line up the places carefully when you add or subtract 4-digit numbers.
Estimate first to check that your answer makes sense.

example.q: A wildlife park counted 1342 deer last year and 1518 deer this year. How many more deer are there this year?

learn.reallife: Forest departments count tigers, elephants and birds to know if the animals are safe and growing in number.

games.title: Add or subtract?
items: Visitors in the morning and evening altogether
How many more deer this year
Birds in two lakes in all
How many fewer leopards than tigers

quiz.q: A wildlife park counted 1342 deer last year and 1518 deer this year. How many more deer are there this year?
quiz.explain: 'How many more' means subtract. 1518 - 1342 = 176.
quiz.mistake: Takes the smaller digit from the bigger in every place

quiz.q: One lake has 2465 birds and another has 3178 birds. How many birds are there in both lakes?
quiz.mistake: Forgets a carry

quiz.q: Visitors to a tiger reserve in 4 months were 4508, 4580, 4085 and 4805. Which is the largest?
quiz.explain: All have 4 thousands. Compare the hundreds: 5, 5, 0, 8. 4805 has 8 hundreds, the most.
quiz.mistake: Looks at the ones digit instead of the hundreds

quiz.q: A forest has 3456 trees. What is the place value of 4 in 3456?
quiz.explain: The 4 is in the hundreds place, so its value is 4 × 100 = 400.
quiz.mistake: Gives the digit itself instead of its place value

quiz.q: A zoo had 2750 visitors in the morning and 1875 in the evening. How many visitors came that day?
quiz.mistake: Forgets to carry into the thousands

quiz.q: A safari park had 3980 visitors in a week. Which is the best estimate?
quiz.explain: 3980 is only 20 less than 4000, so about 4000 is the best estimate.
quiz.mistake: Looks only at the thousands digit and says about 3000

quiz.q: Three elephant herds have 18, 27 and 15 elephants. How many elephants are there in all?
quiz.mistake: Forgets a carry while adding

quiz.q: A tiger reserve wants to plant 5000 saplings. 3275 have been planted. How many are still left to plant?
quiz.mistake: Forgets that borrowing makes the thousands 1 less (gets 2725)

teach.ask: A ranger counted 2465 birds at one lake and 3178 at another. Gappu wants the total. How should Gappu do it?
teach.praise: Great! Line up the places, add from the ones and carry. 5643 birds! Gappu is a ranger now!
teach.nudge: Does 'total' mean add or subtract? Where should Gappu start adding?

learn.hook: A big elephant can eat a huge pile of food every day! How much in a week? Multiply to find out!
points: When the same amount repeats every day or for every animal, multiply.
Break numbers into hundreds, tens and ones: 125 × 7 = 100 × 7 + 20 × 7 + 5 × 7.
To multiply by a 2-digit number, split it: 23 × 12 = 23 × 10 + 23 × 2.
Multiplying by 20 is like multiplying by 2 and then by 10.

example.q: A zoo elephant is given 125 kg of food each day. How much food does it get in 7 days?

learn.reallife: Zoo keepers plan how much food to buy for each animal for a week or a month.

quiz.q: Suppose an elephant drinks 150 litres of water a day. How much does it drink in 4 days?
quiz.mistake: Adds 4 instead of multiplying

quiz.q: A zoo elephant is given 125 kg of food each day. How much food is that in 7 days?
quiz.mistake: Makes a carrying mistake

quiz.q: A tiger cub naps 15 hours a day. How many hours does it nap in 6 days?
quiz.mistake: Adds 15 + 6 instead of multiplying

quiz.q: Each safari jeep carries 6 visitors. 35 jeeps go out in a day. How many visitors go on safari?
quiz.mistake: Multiplies only the tens part (gets 180)

quiz.q: What is 23 × 12?
quiz.mistake: Multiplies by 10 only and forgets the 2

quiz.q: A forest guard walks 14 km every day. How far does she walk in 12 days?
quiz.mistake: Adds 14 + 12 instead of multiplying

quiz.q: A ticket to the leopard safari costs ₹45. How much do 20 children pay altogether?
quiz.mistake: Multiplies by 10 instead of 20 (gets ₹450)

quiz.q: Which is the same as 16 × 25?
quiz.explain: 25 = 20 + 5, so 16 × 25 = 16 × 20 + 16 × 5. Each part must be multiplied by 16.
quiz.mistake: Splits 25 but forgets to multiply the 5 by 16

teach.ask: Gappu wants to find 23 × 12 but it looks too big! How can Gappu make it easier?
teach.praise: Wonderful! 23 × 10 = 230 and 23 × 2 = 46. Add them: 276. Gappu did it!
teach.nudge: Can Gappu split 12 into an easy 10 and a small part?

learn.hook: Some forest puzzles need two steps. Plan first, then solve one step at a time!
points: Read the problem and find what is asked at the end.
Find the hidden first step. For example, find the cost of all the tickets before finding the change.
Do the steps in order and write each answer.
Check: does the final answer make sense?

example.q: A forest has 3 lakes with 45 ducks on each. 28 ducks fly away. How many ducks are left?

learn.reallife: A school trip to a national park needs two-step planning: total ticket cost, then change from the money collected.

games.title: Plan the steps
games.prompt: Put the steps in order: tickets cost ₹125 each. Find the change from ₹1000 for 6 tickets.

quiz.q: A viewing gallery has 4 rows of 25 seats. 63 seats are filled. How many seats are empty?
quiz.explain: Total seats: 4 × 25 = 100. Empty: 100 - 63 = 37.
quiz.mistake: Stops after finding the total seats

quiz.q: Safari tickets cost ₹30 for an adult and ₹15 for a child. How much do 2 adults and 3 children pay?
quiz.mistake: Uses the adult price for everyone or mixes up the numbers

quiz.q: 96 bananas are shared equally among 8 elephants. How many bananas does each elephant get?
quiz.mistake: Takes away 8 from 96

quiz.q: A forest has 3 lakes with 45 ducks on each lake. 28 ducks fly away. How many ducks are left?
quiz.explain: 3 × 45 = 135 ducks. 135 - 28 = 107 ducks left.
quiz.mistake: Makes a borrowing mistake in the second step (gets 117)

quiz.q: A ranger buys 6 bags of seeds at ₹125 each. He pays with ₹1000. How much change does he get?
quiz.mistake: Gives the cost instead of the change

quiz.q: A wildlife park gets 1500 visitors each day it is open. It is closed on Mondays. How many visitors come in one week?
quiz.explain: The park is open 7 - 1 = 6 days. 6 × 1500 = 9000 visitors.
quiz.mistake: Counts all 7 days (gets 10500)

quiz.q: 240 saplings are planted in rows of 12. How many rows are there?
quiz.mistake: Drops the 0 and gets 2 or 24

quiz.q: In a camp, 5 grown-up elephants eat 150 kg each and 2 baby elephants eat 50 kg each in a day. How much food do they eat in all?
quiz.explain: Grown-ups: 5 × 150 = 750 kg. Babies: 2 × 50 = 100 kg. Total: 850 kg.
quiz.mistake: Forgets the baby elephants

teach.ask: Gappu wants to know the change from ₹1000 after buying 6 tickets of ₹125. Gappu is stuck. What first?
teach.praise: Super! First find the cost (6 × 125 = 750), then the change (1000 - 750 = 250). Two steps done!
teach.nudge: What must Gappu find before the change? How much do all the tickets cost?

learn.hook: Fold a butterfly picture down the middle. Both halves match perfectly! That fold is a line of symmetry.
points: A line of symmetry cuts a shape into two halves that match exactly when folded.
Some shapes have one line of symmetry, some have many, and some have none.
A square has 4 lines of symmetry. A rectangle that is not a square has 2.
A triangle with all sides equal has 3 lines of symmetry. A circle has endless lines of symmetry.
Letters like A, T and V have a standing (vertical) line of symmetry. B, C and E have a lying (horizontal) one. F, L, N and S have none.

example.q: How many lines of symmetry does the letter H have?
steps: Fold H from top to bottom down the middle: the halves match.
Fold H from left to right across the middle: the halves match.

learn.reallife: Rangoli, the Taj Mahal from the front, leaves and many logos are symmetrical.

quiz.q: How many lines of symmetry does a square have?
quiz.explain: A square can be folded in half 4 ways: up-down, left-right and along both corner-to-corner lines.
quiz.mistake: Forgets the two corner-to-corner (diagonal) folds

quiz.q: How many lines of symmetry does a rectangle that is not a square have?
quiz.explain: It folds evenly only across the middle in two ways. A corner-to-corner fold does not make the halves match.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the diagonals of a rectangle are lines of symmetry, like in a square

quiz.q: Which letter has a line of symmetry?
quiz.explain: A folds down the middle into two matching halves. F, L and N do not match when folded.
quiz.mistake: Thinks any letter with straight lines is symmetrical

quiz.q: Which letter has NO line of symmetry?
quiz.explain: No fold makes the two halves of S match. H, T and E each have at least one line of symmetry.
quiz.mistake: Thinks S is symmetrical because it looks the same when turned upside down

quiz.q: A triangle has all 3 sides equal. How many lines of symmetry does it have?
quiz.explain: You can fold it from each corner to the middle of the opposite side. That is 3 lines.
quiz.mistake: Finds only the up-down fold

quiz.q: Which letter has a lying (horizontal) line of symmetry, so its top half matches its bottom half?
quiz.explain: B folded from top to bottom matches. A, T and V have only a standing line of symmetry.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up standing (vertical) and lying (horizontal) lines

quiz.q: How many lines of symmetry does the capital letter H have?
quiz.explain: H matches when folded down the middle and when folded across the middle. That is 2 lines.
quiz.mistake: Finds only one of the two folds

quiz.q: Which of these has the most lines of symmetry?
quiz.explain: Any fold through the centre of a circle makes matching halves, so a circle has endless lines of symmetry.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the square has the most because it has 4

teach.ask: Gappu folded a paper heart down the middle and both halves matched! What is that fold line called?
teach.praise: Yes! When both halves match after folding, the fold is a line of symmetry. Gappu loves it!
teach.nudge: What happens to the two halves when Gappu folds? What do we call that line?

learn.hook: Put a mirror on half a picture and, like magic, the whole picture appears!
points: A mirror shows a flipped copy. Left becomes right and right becomes left.
If you know one half of a symmetrical shape, you can draw the other half like a mirror image.
Each point on one side is the same distance from the mirror line as its partner on the other side.
Fold paper, cut a shape on the fold and open it. You get a symmetrical shape!
In a mirror, b looks like d.

example.q: Half of a rangoli has 7 dots on the left of the fold line, and no dots on the line. How many dots are in the whole rangoli?
steps: The right half is a mirror copy of the left half.

learn.reallife: Mehendi designs, kite patterns and paper cut-outs for Diwali use mirror halves.

games.title: Mirror magic
items: In a mirror, your right hand looks like a left hand.
A mirror flips left and right.
The letter b looks like d in a mirror held to its side.
The bump flips to the other side.
The mirror half of a shape can be a different size.
Mirror halves are exactly the same size and shape.
If you cut a half-heart on a fold and open the paper, you get a whole heart.
The fold is the line of symmetry.
The word MOM looks the same in a mirror held to its side.
M and O look the same flipped, and the word reads the same both ways.
The letter F looks the same in a mirror held to its side.
F faces the other way in the mirror.

items.text: Left half has 5 petals and none are on the line. The whole flower has ___ petals.
A half-shape is 3 squares wide. The full shape is ___ squares wide.
In a mirror held to the side, the letter d looks like ___.
A dot is 2 squares to the left of the mirror line. Its mirror dot is 2 squares to the ___.
