quiz.q: Riya folds a paper in half and cuts out half a heart along the fold. What does she get when she opens it?
quiz.explain: The fold is the line of symmetry. Opening it shows both matching halves joined: a whole heart.
quiz.mistake: Does not see that the fold joins the two halves

quiz.q: In a mirror held to its side, what does the letter b look like?
quiz.explain: A mirror flips left and right. The bump of b moves to the left side, making it look like d.
quiz.mistake: Flips it upside down instead of left to right

quiz.q: A symmetrical rangoli has 7 dots on the left of the fold line and none on the line. How many dots are in the whole rangoli?
quiz.explain: The right half is a mirror copy, so it has 7 dots too. 7 + 7 = 14.
quiz.mistake: Counts only one half

quiz.q: Which word looks the same in a mirror held to its side?
quiz.explain: M and O look the same when flipped, and MOM reads the same both ways. B, D, S, N and P do not.
quiz.mistake: Checks only one letter of the word

quiz.q: Which digit looks the same in a mirror held to its side?
quiz.explain: 8 has a standing line of symmetry, so its mirror image is the same. 2, 4 and 7 face the other way.
quiz.mistake: Does not picture the digit flipped left to right

quiz.q: Arjun draws the left half of a symmetrical shape. It is 3 squares wide. How wide is the full shape?
quiz.explain: The right half is the same width as the left half. 3 + 3 = 6 squares.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the half is already the whole shape

quiz.q: A dot is 4 squares to the left of a mirror line. Where is its mirror dot?
options: 4 squares to the right of the line
4 squares to the left of the line
8 squares to the right of the line
quiz.explain: A mirror dot is the same distance from the line but on the other side.
quiz.mistake: Doubles the distance instead of keeping it the same

quiz.q: Kabir stands 2 steps in front of a mirror. How far behind the mirror does his image seem to be?
quiz.explain: Your mirror image always seems to be the same distance behind the mirror as you are in front of it.
quiz.mistake: Adds the two distances together

teach.ask: Gappu has half a butterfly drawing and a mirror. How can Gappu see or draw the whole butterfly?
teach.praise: Magic! Put the mirror on the line and the other half appears, the same but flipped. Gappu's butterfly is complete!
teach.nudge: What does a mirror do to a picture? How is the other half related to the first half?

learn.hook: Tick, tock! The train leaves at 7:05. Can you read the clock and not miss it?
points: The short hand shows the hour. The long hand shows the minutes.
The long hand moves from one number to the next in 5 minutes. So at 4 it shows 20 minutes, at 9 it shows 45 minutes.
Between two numbers there are 5 small marks. Each small mark is 1 minute.
Quarter past 6 is 6:15. Half past 6 is 6:30. Quarter to 7 is 6:45.
We write minutes with two digits: 7 o'clock and 5 minutes is 7:05.

example.q: The short hand is between 4 and 5. The long hand is 2 small marks after the 7. What time is it?
steps: Hour: the short hand has passed 4, so the hour is 4.

learn.reallife: We read clocks to catch the school bus, start a cricket match or know when our favourite show begins.

items.q: Long hand on 3: how many minutes past?
Long hand on 6: how many minutes past?
Long hand on 8: how many minutes past?
Long hand on 11: how many minutes past?
Long hand 3 small marks after 2: minutes past?
Long hand on 1: how many minutes past?

quiz.q: The short hand is just past 3 and the long hand is on 4. What time is it?
quiz.explain: The short hand shows 3 o'clock has passed. The long hand on 4 means 4 × 5 = 20 minutes. So it is 3:20.
quiz.mistake: Reads the long hand number as the minutes (3:04) or mixes up the hands

quiz.q: The long hand points to 9. How many minutes past the hour is it?
quiz.explain: Each number on the clock is 5 minutes for the long hand. 9 × 5 = 45 minutes.
quiz.mistake: Reads the number 9 as 9 minutes

quiz.q: What time is 'quarter past 6'?
quiz.explain: A quarter of an hour is 15 minutes. Quarter past 6 is 15 minutes after 6: 6:15.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up quarter past and quarter to

quiz.q: What time is 'half past 11'?
quiz.explain: Half an hour is 30 minutes. Half past 11 is 11:30.
quiz.mistake: Thinks half past means 50 minutes

quiz.q: The clock shows 8:50. How else can we say this time?
quiz.explain: 8:50 is 10 minutes before 9:00, so it is 10 minutes to 9.
quiz.mistake: Uses the hour that has passed instead of the coming hour

quiz.q: How many minutes are there in 1 hour?
quiz.explain: The long hand goes all the way round once in 60 minutes. That is 1 hour.
quiz.mistake: Thinks an hour has 100 minutes, like a metre has 100 cm

quiz.q: The short hand is between 4 and 5. The long hand is 2 small marks after the 7. What time is it?
quiz.explain: The hour is 4. The long hand at 7 means 35 minutes, and 2 more marks make 37. So 4:37.
quiz.mistake: Writes the 7 and the 2 side by side

quiz.q: The train leaves at 7 o'clock and 5 minutes. How do we write this time?
quiz.explain: Minutes are written with two digits. 5 minutes is written as 05, so 7:05.
quiz.mistake: Writes 7:50, which is 50 minutes past 7

teach.ask: Gappu sees the long hand on 4 and says it is 4 minutes past. Is Gappu right?
teach.praise: Thank you! Each number is 5 minutes for the long hand, so 4 means 20 minutes. Gappu reads clocks now!
teach.nudge: How many minutes does the long hand take to go from one number to the next?

topics.title: How long does it take? Time durations

learn.hook: School starts at 8:00 am and ends at 1:30 pm. How long are you in school? Let's count the time!
points: am is for times from midnight to noon (morning). pm is for times from noon to midnight (afternoon and night).
1 hour = 60 minutes. 2 hours = 120 minutes.
To find how long, count on: first to the next full hour, then the hours, then the minutes.
To find the end time, add the time taken to the start time. If minutes reach 60, change them into 1 hour.

example.q: A cricket match on TV goes from 2:40 pm to 4:10 pm. How long is it?

learn.reallife: We work out how long a train journey takes, or how long we can play before dinner.

items.text: 2 hours = ___ minutes
3:15 pm + 2 hours = ___
90 minutes = 1 hour ___ minutes

quiz.q: School starts at 8:00 am and ends at 1:30 pm. How long is the school day?
quiz.explain: 8:00 am to 12:00 noon is 4 hours. 12:00 to 1:30 pm is 1 hour 30 minutes. Total: 5 hours 30 minutes.
quiz.mistake: Counts from 8 to 1 wrongly by forgetting that 12 comes before 1

quiz.q: How many minutes are there in 2 hours?
quiz.explain: 1 hour = 60 minutes. 2 × 60 = 120 minutes.
quiz.mistake: Thinks 1 hour is 100 minutes

quiz.q: A film starts at 3:15 pm and lasts 2 hours. When does it end?
quiz.explain: Add 2 hours to 3:15 pm: 4:15 pm, then 5:15 pm. It is still afternoon, so pm.
quiz.mistake: Changes pm to am, or adds 2 minutes

quiz.q: Arjun eats breakfast at 7 o'clock in the morning. How do we write this time?
quiz.explain: Morning times before noon use am. So it is 7:00 am.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up am and pm

quiz.q: A cricket match on TV goes from 2:40 pm to 4:10 pm. How long is it?
quiz.explain: 2:40 to 3:00 is 20 minutes, 3:00 to 4:00 is 60 minutes, 4:00 to 4:10 is 10 minutes. 20 + 60 + 10 = 90.
quiz.mistake: Subtracts 410 - 240 like ordinary numbers (gets 170)

quiz.q: Riya sleeps at 9:30 pm and wakes up at 6:30 am. How long does she sleep?
quiz.explain: 9:30 pm to 12:00 midnight is 2 hours 30 minutes. Midnight to 6:30 am is 6 hours 30 minutes. Together: 9 hours.
quiz.mistake: Subtracts 9:30 - 6:30 and forgets the time goes past midnight

quiz.q: How many hours and minutes is 90 minutes?
quiz.explain: 60 minutes make 1 hour. 90 - 60 = 30. So 90 minutes = 1 hour 30 minutes.
quiz.mistake: Thinks 1 hour is 40 minutes or divides by 10

quiz.q: A clock shows 10:45. What time will it be 20 minutes later?
quiz.explain: 10:45 + 15 minutes = 11:00. 5 more minutes makes 11:05.
quiz.mistake: Adds 45 + 20 = 65 and writes 10:65

teach.ask: Gappu's train leaves at 2:40 pm and arrives at 4:10 pm. Gappu did 410 - 240 = 170 minutes. Is that right?
teach.praise: Aha! An hour has 60 minutes, not 100. Count on: 20 + 60 + 10 = 90 minutes!
teach.nudge: How many minutes are in an hour? Try counting on to 3:00 first.

learn.hook: Your birthday is coming! How many days to wait? The calendar knows!
points: A week has 7 days. A year has 12 months.
April, June, September and November have 30 days. February has 28 days (29 in a leap year). All the other months have 31 days.
A year has 365 days. A leap year has 366 days.
The same day of the week comes again every 7 days. If 1 June is a Monday, so are 8, 15, 22 and 29 June.
To count days to a date in the next month, count to the end of this month, then add the days of the next month.

example.q: Today is 28 March. Aisha's birthday is on 5 April. How many days does she have to wait?
steps: March has 31 days. From 28 March to 31 March is 31 - 28 = 3 days.
Then 5 more days to reach 5 April.

learn.reallife: We use calendars to plan holidays, mark exams, count days to Diwali and remember birthdays.

games.title: Calendar facts
items: February gets an extra day, the 29th.
If 1 June is a Monday, then 8 June is also a Monday.
In a year that is not a leap year, February has 28 days.
Only a leap year gives February 29 days.

quiz.q: How many days are there in March?
quiz.explain: March is one of the months with 31 days.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up March with a 30-day month

quiz.q: In a year that is not a leap year, how many days does February have?
quiz.explain: February is the shortest month. It has 28 days, and 29 only in a leap year.
quiz.mistake: Gives the leap-year number of days

quiz.q: How many days are there in a year that is not a leap year?
quiz.explain: An ordinary year has 365 days. A leap year has 366.
quiz.mistake: Thinks every month has 30 days (12 × 30 = 360)

quiz.q: 1 June is a Monday. What day is 8 June?
quiz.explain: 8 June is 7 days after 1 June. The day of the week repeats every 7 days, so it is Monday again.
quiz.mistake: Counts 8 days ahead instead of 7

quiz.q: Today is Friday. What day will it be 3 days from today?
quiz.explain: Count on: Saturday (1), Sunday (2), Monday (3).
quiz.mistake: Counts today as one of the 3 days

quiz.q: How many weeks are there in 28 days?
quiz.explain: Each week has 7 days. 28 ÷ 7 = 4 weeks.
quiz.mistake: Takes away 7 from 28 instead of dividing

quiz.q: Today is 28 March. Aisha's birthday is on 5 April. How many days does she have to wait?
quiz.explain: 28 March to 31 March is 3 days, then 5 more days to 5 April. 3 + 5 = 8 days.
quiz.mistake: Thinks March has 30 days (gets 7)

quiz.q: Which of these months has 30 days?
quiz.explain: April has 30 days. May, January and August each have 31 days.
quiz.mistake: Forgets which months have 30 days

teach.ask: Today is 25 May and Gappu's party is on 2 June. Gappu thinks it's 7 days away. How do we count?
teach.praise: Yes! May has 31 days: 25 to 31 is 6 days, then 2 more makes 8 days. Gappu is excited!
teach.nudge: How many days does May have? Count to the end of May first.

learn.hook: The ticket to the transport museum costs ₹75. Which notes and coins will you give?
points: ₹1 = 100 paise.
₹5.50 means 5 rupees and 50 paise. The dot separates rupees from paise.
We have notes like ₹10, ₹20, ₹50, ₹100, ₹200 and ₹500, and coins like ₹1, ₹2, ₹5, ₹10 and ₹20.
To count money, start with the biggest notes, then add the smaller ones.
There are many ways to make the same amount. ₹75 = ₹50 + ₹20 + ₹5.

example.q: Kabir has four ₹20 notes and three ₹5 coins. How much money does he have?

learn.reallife: We count money when buying tickets, snacks at the station or souvenirs at a museum shop.

quiz.q: How many paise make ₹1?
quiz.explain: 1 rupee is the same as 100 paise.
quiz.mistake: Thinks ₹1 is 10 paise

quiz.q: Joseph has three ₹500 notes and two ₹100 notes. How much money does he have?
quiz.mistake: Counts only the ₹500 notes

quiz.q: How many ₹10 coins make ₹100?
quiz.mistake: Thinks 100 coins are needed

quiz.q: How do we write 5 rupees and 50 paise?
quiz.explain: Rupees go before the dot and paise after it: ₹5.50.
quiz.mistake: Writes 50 paise as .05

quiz.q: The museum ticket costs ₹75. Which set of money makes exactly ₹75?
quiz.mistake: Does not add up each set carefully

quiz.q: How many rupees is 250 paise?
quiz.explain: 100 paise = ₹1. 250 paise = ₹2 and 50 paise = ₹2.50.
quiz.mistake: Divides by 10 instead of 100

quiz.q: Riya must pay ₹700 using only ₹500 and ₹100 notes. What is the smallest number of notes she can use?
quiz.explain: One ₹500 note and two ₹100 notes make ₹700. That is 1 + 2 = 3 notes.
quiz.mistake: Uses only ₹100 notes (7 notes)

quiz.q: Kabir has four ₹20 notes and three ₹5 coins. How much money does he have?
quiz.mistake: Counts only one ₹5 coin (gets ₹85)

teach.ask: Gappu found 150 paise in the piggy bank. Gappu thinks it is ₹150. Is that right?
teach.praise: Oh! 100 paise make ₹1, so 150 paise is ₹1.50, not ₹150. Thank you!
teach.nudge: How many paise make one rupee?

learn.hook: At the museum shop you buy toy trains and postcards. The shopkeeper gives you a bill. Can you check it?
points: A bill lists each item, how many (quantity), the price of one (rate) and the amount.
Amount = quantity × rate. 3 toy trains at ₹45 each = 3 × 45 = ₹135.
Add all the amounts to get the total.
Always check a bill. Shopkeepers can make mistakes too!
Change = money given - total.

example.q: Bill: 5 pencils at ₹6 each and 2 erasers at ₹5 each. What is the total?

learn.reallife: Grocery shops, restaurants and railway ticket counters all give bills.

items.text: Qty 4, Rate ₹25, Amount ₹___
Qty 3, Rate ₹45, Amount ₹___
Qty 2, Rate ₹120, Amount ₹___
Total ₹385, paid ₹500, change ₹___

games.title: Is the bill right?
items: Multiply how many by the price of one.
Change from ₹500 for a ₹385 bill is ₹125

quiz.q: Meena buys 3 toy trains at ₹45 each. What is the amount?
quiz.explain: Amount = quantity × rate = 3 × ₹45 = ₹135.
quiz.mistake: Adds 3 + 45 instead of multiplying

quiz.q: A bill has 5 pencils at ₹6 each and 2 erasers at ₹5 each. What is the total?
quiz.explain: Pencils: 5 × 6 = ₹30. Erasers: 2 × 5 = ₹10. Total = ₹40.
quiz.mistake: Forgets to add the erasers

quiz.q: On a bill, what does 'rate' mean?
quiz.explain: Rate is the price of one item. Amount = quantity × rate.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up rate with amount or quantity

quiz.q: Apples cost ₹120 per kg. Aisha buys 2 kg. What is the amount?
quiz.mistake: Adds 2 instead of multiplying by 2

quiz.q: A bill line says: Qty 4, Rate ₹25. What should the amount be?
quiz.explain: 4 × 25 = 100. So the amount is ₹100.
quiz.mistake: Adds quantity and rate

quiz.q: A bill says 3 postcards × ₹40 = ₹130. What should the correct amount be?
quiz.explain: 3 × 40 = 120, so the bill should say ₹120. The shopkeeper made a mistake.
quiz.mistake: Trusts the bill without checking

quiz.q: At the transport museum, adult tickets cost ₹50 and child tickets cost ₹20. What is the bill for 2 adults and 3 children?
quiz.explain: Adults: 2 × 50 = ₹100. Children: 3 × 20 = ₹60. Total: ₹160.
quiz.mistake: Adds one adult and one child ticket only (₹70)

quiz.q: Harpreet's bill total is ₹385. She pays with a ₹500 note. How much change should she get?
quiz.mistake: Makes a borrowing mistake (gets ₹125)

teach.ask: Gappu bought 4 toy cars at ₹25 each. The bill says ₹125. How can Gappu check the bill?
teach.praise: Well done! 4 × 25 = 100, so the bill should be ₹100. Gappu saved ₹25!
teach.nudge: How do we find the amount from the number of cars and the price of one?

learn.hook: Saving for a model train? Sharing a taxi fare? Money maths helps every day!
points: Add to find a total cost. Subtract to find what is left or how much more is needed.
Multiply when the same price repeats. Divide to share money equally.
When adding rupees and paise, 100 paise make ₹1: ₹10.50 + ₹4.50 = ₹15.00.
To compare deals, find the price of one item in each.

example.q: Joseph has ₹200. A toy bus costs ₹135. How much money will he have left?

learn.reallife: Families share expenses for a trip, save money every week and compare prices before buying.

games.title: Which operation?
items: Savings of ₹25 a week for 8 weeks
How much more is needed to buy a bicycle
Cost of a samosa and a juice together

quiz.q: Joseph has ₹200. A toy bus costs ₹135. How much money will he have left?
quiz.mistake: Makes a borrowing mistake (gets ₹75)

quiz.q: ₹360 is shared equally among 4 friends. How much does each get?
quiz.mistake: Takes away 4 instead of dividing

quiz.q: Which is cheaper per pen: a pack of 3 pens for ₹30 or 1 pen for ₹12?
options: Both cost the same per pen
quiz.explain: In the pack each pen costs 30 ÷ 3 = ₹10, which is less than ₹12.
quiz.mistake: Thinks ₹12 is cheaper because it is a smaller number than ₹30

quiz.q: A toy train ride ticket costs ₹85. How much do 6 tickets cost?
quiz.mistake: Multiplies only the tens part (gets ₹480)

quiz.q: Meena saves ₹25 every week. How much will she save in 8 weeks?
quiz.mistake: Adds 25 + 8

quiz.q: A bicycle costs ₹1250. Arjun has ₹875. How much more money does he need?
quiz.mistake: Adds the two amounts instead of subtracting
Forgets that 100 paise make ₹1

quiz.q: Harpreet buys 2 samosas at ₹15 each and 1 juice for ₹25. She pays with ₹100. How much change does she get?
quiz.mistake: Gives the cost instead of the change, or counts only one samosa

teach.ask: Gappu wants to share ₹120 equally with 2 friends, so 3 in all. How much should each get?
teach.praise: Great! ₹120 ÷ 3 = ₹40 each. Fair sharing makes good friends!
teach.nudge: How many people share the money, counting Gappu? What operation shares equally?

learn.hook: Which fruit does your class love most? Don't guess. Ask everyone and count. That's data!
points: Data is information we collect, like answers to a question or things we count.
We can collect data by asking people (a survey) or by watching and counting.
Tally marks help us count fast: 4 lines and a 5th line across make a bundle of 5.
We put the counts in a table so it is easy to read and compare.
From a table we can find the most, the least, the total and the difference.

example.q: In a survey, 12 children chose mango, 8 chose banana and 5 chose apple. How many children took part, and which fruit is the favourite?
steps: The biggest count is 12, for mango.

learn.reallife: Teachers collect data on attendance. Cricket scorers keep data on runs and wickets.

games.title: Data facts
items: A survey means asking people questions and noting their answers.
That is one way to collect data.
In tally marks, the 5th line goes across the other 4.
Guessing is a good way to collect data.
We must ask or count to get real data.
A table makes data easier to read.
Counts are neatly lined up to compare.
If mango has 12 votes and apple has 5, apple is more popular.
12 is more than 5, so mango is more popular.

quiz.q: Arjun's tally for red cars has 2 bundles of five and 3 more lines. How many red cars did he count?
quiz.explain: 2 bundles of five = 10. 3 more lines make 13.
quiz.mistake: Counts each bundle as 1

quiz.q: In a survey, 12 children chose mango, 8 chose banana and 5 chose apple. How many children took part?
quiz.explain: 12 + 8 + 5 = 25 children.
quiz.mistake: Adds only two of the fruits

quiz.q: In the same survey (mango 12, banana 8, apple 5), which fruit is the favourite?
quiz.explain: Mango has the biggest count, 12.
quiz.mistake: Picks the fruit with the smallest count

quiz.q: How many more children chose mango (12) than apple (5)?
quiz.explain: 12 - 5 = 7 more children chose mango.
quiz.mistake: Adds the two numbers instead of finding the difference

quiz.q: Riya wants to know how her classmates come to school. What is the best way to collect this data?
options: Ask each child and make tally marks
Guess from looking at the gate once
Count the bicycles at her home
quiz.explain: Asking every child and keeping a tally gives correct, complete data.
quiz.mistake: Thinks asking one person or guessing is enough

quiz.q: A table of favourite colours shows Red 9, Blue 6, Green 9, Yellow 4. Which two colours got the same number of votes?
quiz.explain: Red and Green both have 9 votes.
quiz.mistake: Reads the table rows carelessly

quiz.q: Kabir counted vehicles passing his school: 14 cars, 23 bikes and 9 buses. How many vehicles did he count?
quiz.explain: 14 + 23 + 9 = 46 vehicles.
quiz.mistake: Forgets to add the buses

quiz.q: In Kabir's count (14 cars, 23 bikes, 9 buses), how many fewer buses than bikes were there?
quiz.explain: 23 - 9 = 14 fewer buses.
quiz.mistake: Adds the two numbers instead of subtracting

teach.ask: Gappu wants to know the favourite sweet of all the birds in the forest. How should Gappu find out?
teach.praise: Yes! Ask everyone, count with tally marks and write it in a table. Gappu will find the favourite sweet!
teach.nudge: Should Gappu just guess? What should Gappu do with each answer?

learn.hook: Can a picture of one star stand for 5 children? In a pictograph it can!
points: A pictograph shows data using pictures or symbols.
The key tells how much one symbol stands for, like ⭐ = 5 children.
To read a row, multiply the number of symbols by the key value.
Half a symbol stands for half the key value. If ⭐ = 4, half a star = 2.
To draw a row, divide the number by the key value to find how many symbols.

example.q: Key: each ⭐ = 5 children. The cricket row has 4 stars. How many children like cricket?

learn.reallife: Newspapers and school notice boards use pictographs to show data in a fun way.

items.q: Key 🌟 = 4. Row has 2 and a half 🌟

items.text: Key 🪁 = 5 kites. To show 25 kites, draw ___ symbols.
Key 🚌 = 10 children. To show 40 children, draw ___ symbols.
Key 🍪 = 4 cookies. To show 12 cookies, draw ___ symbols.
Key ⭐ = 2 votes. Half a star stands for ___ vote.

quiz.q: Key: each ⭐ = 5 children. The cricket row has 4 stars. How many children like cricket?
quiz.explain: 4 stars × 5 children = 20 children.
quiz.mistake: Counts the stars but forgets the key

quiz.q: Key: each ⚽ = 10 children. The football row has 3 balls. How many children like football?
quiz.explain: 3 × 10 = 30 children.
quiz.mistake: Adds the key value instead of multiplying

quiz.q: Key: each 🪁 = 5 kites. A shop sold 25 kites. How many kite symbols should the row have?
quiz.explain: 25 ÷ 5 = 5 symbols.
quiz.mistake: Draws one symbol for every kite

quiz.q: Key: each 🍪 = 4 cookies. A row shows 3 full cookies and half a cookie. How many cookies is that?
quiz.explain: 3 full symbols = 3 × 4 = 12. Half a symbol = 2. 12 + 2 = 14.
quiz.mistake: Ignores the half symbol, or counts it as a full one

quiz.q: Key: each 📚 = 10 books. Monday has 2 symbols and Tuesday has 5 symbols. How many more books were borrowed on Tuesday?
quiz.explain: Tuesday has 5 - 2 = 3 more symbols. 3 × 10 = 30 more books.
quiz.mistake: Gives the difference in symbols (3) instead of books

quiz.q: Why does a pictograph need a key?
options: To tell how much one symbol stands for
quiz.explain: The key tells us the value of one symbol, so we can read the numbers.
quiz.mistake: Thinks each symbol always means 1

quiz.q: Key: each 🚌 = 10 children. How should 40 children be shown?
quiz.explain: 40 ÷ 10 = 4, so draw 4 bus symbols.
quiz.mistake: Draws one symbol for each child

quiz.q: Key: each 😊 = 3 children. Class A has 4 symbols and Class B has 6 symbols. How many children are there in both classes?
quiz.explain: 4 + 6 = 10 symbols. 10 × 3 = 30 children.
quiz.mistake: Counts symbols without using the key

teach.ask: Gappu sees a pictograph with 5 apple pictures but the key says 🍎 = 2 apples. Gappu says 5 apples. Is that right?
teach.praise: Thanks! Each picture is 2 apples, so 5 × 2 = 10 apples. Always read the key!
teach.nudge: What does the key tell Gappu about each apple picture?

learn.hook: Tall bars, short bars! A bar graph lets you compare data in one quick look.
points: A bar graph uses bars to show data. A taller (or longer) bar means a bigger number.
Read the number at the end of each bar using the scale on the side.
The scale can go up in 1s, 2s, 5s or 10s. Check it before reading!
We can use a bar graph to find the most, the least, the total and the difference.

example.q: A bar graph shows rangoli kits sold: Monday 4, Tuesday 7, Wednesday 3, Thursday 6. Which day sold the most, and how many were sold in all?

learn.reallife: TV news shows bar graphs of rainfall, cricket runs per over and votes.

games.title: Bar graph facts
items: A taller bar shows a bigger number.
The height of a bar shows the amount.
The scale on a bar graph must always go up in 1s.
It can go up in 2s, 5s, 10s and so on.
Two bars of the same height show the same number.
The shortest bar shows the most popular choice.
The tallest bar shows the most popular choice.
If each line stands for 2, a bar reaching the 6th line shows 12.

quiz.q: A bar graph shows rangoli kits sold: Mon 4, Tue 7, Wed 3, Thu 6. On which day were the most kits sold?
quiz.explain: Tuesday has the tallest bar, 7 kits.
quiz.mistake: Picks the day with the shortest bar

quiz.q: Rangoli kits sold were Mon 4, Tue 7, Wed 3, Thu 6. How many more kits were sold on Tuesday than on Wednesday?
quiz.explain: 7 - 3 = 4 more kits on Tuesday.
quiz.mistake: Adds the two bars instead of finding the difference

quiz.q: Rangoli kits sold were Mon 4, Tue 7, Wed 3, Thu 6. How many kits were sold in the 4 days altogether?
quiz.mistake: Misses one of the bars

quiz.q: A bar graph of favourite games shows Cricket 15, Kabaddi 10, Kho-kho 5, Football 10. Which two games have bars of the same height?
quiz.explain: Kabaddi and Football both have 10 votes, so their bars are the same height.
quiz.mistake: Does not read the bar values carefully

quiz.q: On a bar graph, each line on the scale stands for 2 students. A bar reaches the 6th line. How many students does it show?
quiz.explain: 6 lines × 2 students = 12 students.
quiz.mistake: Reads the line number without using the scale

quiz.q: In the favourite games graph (Cricket 15, Kabaddi 10, Kho-kho 5, Football 10), which game is liked the least?
quiz.explain: Kho-kho has the shortest bar, only 5 votes.
quiz.mistake: Picks the tallest bar instead of the shortest

quiz.q: What does a taller bar in a bar graph show?
quiz.explain: The taller the bar, the bigger the number it shows.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the bar height has no meaning

quiz.q: A bar graph shows rainy days: June 8, July 15, August 12, September 6. How many rainy days were there in July and August together?
quiz.explain: 15 + 12 = 27 rainy days.
quiz.mistake: Finds the difference instead of the total

teach.ask: Gappu sees a bar graph of fruits but doesn't know how to read it. What should Gappu look at?
teach.praise: Thank you! Taller bars mean more, and the scale tells the exact number. Gappu can read graphs now!
teach.nudge: What does a taller bar mean? Where does Gappu read the number?
